articles.title: 2026-27 Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft: Round-by-round analysis for a 12-team Yahoo standard points league
articles.summary: Dan Titus recaps a 12-team standard Yahoo points league mock draft with round-by-round fantasy basketball analysis.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season tips off in two weeks, and I just wrapped a 12-team Yahoo points mock draft with some of the sharpest fantasy basketball minds in the industry. The league uses Yahoo's default points scoring and roster spots . Twelve fantasy basketball analysts, 13 rounds and one big lesson: in Yahoo points leagues, the run on centers comes later than you think, and it comes fast.

All rankings referenced below are my standard points rankings , and ADP is Yahoo's as of Oct. 1 . Let's dive into how it all played out over 13 rounds.

Steve St. Pierre - Menace Podmen Podcast

Karan Talwar - Spreadsheet Fantasy Basketball

Team Papi went Nikola Jokić over Victor Wembanyama at the 1.01, and in points leagues that's the right call. Wemby has the edge in Yahoo ADP (1.6 to 1.9), but Jokić projects for 63.1 fantasy points per game in my numbers, nearly 4.0 points clear of Wemby. Assists count 1.5 points each in this format, and nobody piles them up like the Joker.

The rest of the round went mostly by the book, with a clear lean toward guards. Six of the 12 picks were PG-eligible, while Jokić, Wemby and Giannis Antetokounmpo were the only bigs. Jalen Johnson and Cooper Flagg going back-to-back at 9 and 10 makes sense, too. Both fill up every column of the box score, which is exactly what you want in points.

My pick: I took Tyrese Haliburton at No. 11, which lines up with my rankings. I wanted to start with a high-assist guard who gets steals. Haliburton projects for 9.3 assists against just 1.9 turnovers per game, and that ratio is great in a format that rewards dimes and penalizes giveaways. He's coming off a missed season, so I'm projecting him for about 65 games, but I'd rather take that swing at the 1-2 turn than settle for a safer player with a lower ceiling.

The guard run kept going. Seven of the 12 picks in Round 2 were PG-eligible, capped by four straight from picks 22 through 25: Jalen Brunson, Devin Booker, Jamal Murray and Trae Young to open Round 3. Team Papi pairing Jokić with Murray is a cool stack, and adding Trae at the 3.01 gives that roster a ton of assist volume.

Team Karan grabbing Josh Giddey at 15 caught my eye. Giddey's ADP is around 24, but his 16.9/8.0/9.1 projected line plays way up in points (41.4 FPPG). He's a better points player than a 9-cat one, and that pick told us Team Karan came in with a plan. More on that in a bit.

My pick: Donovan Mitchell at 14 lined up perfectly with both my rankings (13th) and his ADP (13.6). He's averaged at least 24 points in each of the last four seasons, and last year was one of his best: 27.9 points, 5.7 assists and 1.5 steals on 48% shooting over 70 games, good for 44.3 fantasy points per game in Yahoo's default scoring. I'm projecting a small step back this season to 26 points, 5.1 assists and 1.4 steals (42.4 FPPG) over 69 games, which still makes him a top-15 player in points leagues. I considered Giddey here, but I already had my primary playmaker in Haliburton and wanted a high-volume scorer next to him.

This is where the first wave of bigs hit. Evan Mobley, Anthony Davis and Bam Adebayo went back-to-back-to-back at picks 26 through 28, then Domantas Sabonis went at 31 and Jalen Duren at 33. That's five C-eligible players in one round after just six total in Rounds 1 and 2.

AD at 27 went 15 spots ahead of his ADP (42.7), but I'm not calling that a reach. I have him 15th overall, and his 48.1 projected FPPG is the best of anyone in this round. The catch is availability, which is why he'll continue sliding in drafts.

Two Sixers (Jaylen Brown and LeBron James) went in the same round. I have James ahead of Brown by almost 20 picks, so it's interesting to see how others view how the production could shake out with so much talent in Philly.

My pick: With the bigs I wanted gone in that 26-33 stretch, I pivoted to LeBron James at 35. I have him 19th, and Yahoo ADP has him 36th, so this was a 16-spot discount on my board. LeBron is projected for a 20-6.5-7.5 line in Philly, and that breadth of stats will be solid for points leagues. 'Bron is reportedly dealing with arthritis in his foot (who isn't at 41 years old), so the risk is games played (63 in my projection), but at the end of Round 3, I'll take that bet in a points league.

The second wave of bigs followed right behind. Chet Holmgren went at 37, Walker Kessler at 42 and Donovan Clingan at 44. Kessler and Clingan are perfect examples of why centers carry so much value in points: Kessler projects for only 13.3 points per game, but his 11.3 rebounds and 2.5 blocks push him to 38.7 FPPG. Clingan's projection is nearly identical (38.7 FPPG).

Through four rounds, three teams still didn't have a single C-eligible player: Team Adam (Jayson Tatum, Austin Reaves, Jaylen Brown, Jalen Williams), Team Karan (Flagg, Giddey, Kawhi Leonard, Deni Avdija) and mine. Every other team had at least one big, and Team Dunne already drafted two (Sabonis, Kessler). Remember, you have to start at least two centers in Yahoo default leagues, and Dunne made a point of securing a couple of top-tier centers in his first 50 picks.

My pick: Stephon Castle at 38 was one of my favorite values in the draft. I have him 26th, and his Yahoo ADP is 53.9. I'm projecting another step forward for the third-year pro, with my numbers having him at 18-5-7 with over a steal per game, while suiting up for at least 70 games. I know I'm higher than the market on Castle. Remember he's the top assist man for Wemby and that'll go a long way.

Round 5 was a mixed bag, with every position represented. Team SteveSaintP made Cameron Boozer the first rookie off the board at 51, a few picks ahead of his ADP (55.9). His projected 16.8 points and 8.0 rebounds should hold up in points, but I have him 69th, so that's a bit rich for me.

Joel Embiid at 58 was the first big for Team Karan. Embiid is still a per-game monster (41.6 projected FPPG), but my projection only has him for 48 games. In the fifth round, that's a fair price. Embiid is at his lowest weight since his rookie season, so hopefully he can buck his trend of missing a bulk of the season because of injury.

My pick: I still didn't have a big, and Julius Randle at 59 was the best player on my board. I have him 41st, and his ADP is 68.8. He's not flashy, but he produces, and he'll have a ton of usage and opportunities to generate counting stats playing with Michael Porter Jr. and a young Nets team.

Here's the biggest takeaway from this draft: the center run hit in Round 6. From pick 62 through 79, 10 of 18 picks were C-eligible: Ivica Zubac, Zach Edey, Jarrett Allen, Onyeka Okongwu, Rudy Gobert, Naz Reid, Alex Sarr, Kel'el Ware, Derik Queen and Zion Williamson. By the time it was over, the tier of starting centers projected for 35-plus FPPG were gone.

If you're planning to wait on centers in a points league, this is your deadline. Plan to have your starting C locked in by the middle of Round 6, because the next tier comes with a lot more risk.

Okongwu went 14 picks after his ADP (54.9), and he's my 54th-ranked player, so Team Raphielle got a nice discount at 69.

My pick: Six rounds in and my only center-eligible player was Randle. To build out my frontcourt a bit, I grabbed Ivica Zubac at 62. A double-double shouldn't be an issue and I secured the Hali-Zubac stack. I'm projecting Zu to put up 14.8 points and 11.2 rebounds on 63% shooting, good for 38.1 FPPG. I reached by my own numbers, but I knew the run was coming. Edey and Allen were gone within three picks, so I don't regret it.

The run kept going into Round 7, with Sarr, Ware and Queen off the board in the first five picks. Zion Williamson at 79 is a pick I really like for Team Dunne. I have Zion 42nd, and he's projected for 37.9 FPPG. His availability is always a question, but in Round 7, you're getting paid to take that risk.

The biggest faller of the entire draft came at 81. Kon Knueppel went 33 spots after his Yahoo ADP (47.6). That's not a market mistake in points leagues, though. I have Knueppel 79th because he'll miss the entire preseason with a hamstring injury and efficiency not factoring into scoring neutralizes one of his greatest attributes in fantasy. He's a much better 9-cat player than a points one.

My pick: De'Aaron Fox at 83 was another value on my board. I have him 57th, so he lasted 26 spots past where I'd take him. I think he's falling in drafts because drafters remember how bad he was on the biggest stage. However, he was injured and in the regular season he was more than solid in his first full season with the Spurs. In my opinion, buying into two Spurs guards is never a bad idea.

The rookies started flying off the board. Team Justin took Caleb Wilson at 84 and AJ Dybantsa at 85, and he wasn't done (Darryn Peterson in Round 10, second-year player Ace Bailey in Round 11). That's the most youth-heavy build in the league. Dybantsa went a few picks after his ADP (79.1), but I have him 102nd, so I'm lower than the market on his first-year production. The rookies Justin selected are all score-first guys who will likely miss a ton of shots. Points leagues insulate against that, so as long as they're getting minutes with a defined role, they could be useful in points formats in the later rounds.

Nic Claxton (91) and Myles Turner (95) were the last of the starting-caliber centers. Team SteveSaintP took Collin Murray-Boyles at 94, a big jump from his spot in Yahoo ADP (145th). I have CMB 116th, but I'm cool with it, given how I think he's one of the best sleepers in fantasy this season. Avoid Claxton unless he falls to an ungodly level, but he won't be re-evaluated for two weeks. He'll miss time and rather than stash him, pick someone else in that range who can produce fantasy points now.

My pick: I think this is an overcorrection falling this low. I took Ja Morant at 86th overall but I have him 45th, and his Yahoo ADP is 90th. The market still doesn't trust him and rightfully so. Still, Morant is more than capable of averaging 20-3-7 and is coming at a pretty affordable price. He's boom-or-bust, but this is the round to take that shot. If he stays healthy, he's a top-50 points player or possibly higher.

Managers who waited on bigs went back to the well for a mini-run: Isaiah Hartenstein, Jabari Smith Jr., Day'Ron Sharpe and Neemias Queta went back-to-back at picks 99 through 102. Queta at 102 was a modest reach (Yahoo ADP: 117), but in points, a center projected for 7.7 rebounds and 1.2 blocks will make it to 12-team leagues.

DeMar DeRozan at 98 was another early pick by Yahoo ADP (107.4). While that one lines up with my board (I have him ranked 97th), I'm fading DeRozan with him coming off the bench. Rookie Darius Acuff Jr. at 103 is a pick I like. I have him 87th, ahead of his ADP of 109.6.

My pick: RJ Barrett at 107 was my best value left. I have him 83rd, and he sits 112th in Yahoo ADP. He's often overlooked, especially in points formats where he can just do him and not worry about the turnovers, poor FT percentage and his shot not falling at times. Adding Kawhi should help draw more defensive attention, which should work out well for Barrett.

From here on, ADP basically went out the window. Picks in Rounds 1 through 3 landed within about four spots of their Yahoo ADP on average. By Rounds 10 through 13, the average gap was 25 spots. Part of that is how Yahoo ADP works late in drafts (values bunch up between about 116 and 121), but most of it is managers targeting their guys.

The best lesson of the late rounds came at pick 120. Team Papi took Jusuf Nurkić, who projects for 34.4 FPPG. Compare that to the guards taken around him: Davion Mitchell (117) projects for 23.1 FPPG and Jeremiah Fears (111) for 26.5. In points leagues, a late-round big gives you a lot more production than a late-round guard. Team Papi ended up with six C-eligible players, the most in the draft, and Jokić is only one of them.

My pick: This is one spot where Yahoo ADP and I disagree. I took Keegan Murray at 110, and he sits 120th in Yahoo ADP. On my board, he's 107th, so I got him three spots late. Murray is projected for 34.4 minutes per game with 6 rebounds and nearly one steal and one block, good for 31.5 FPPG. That's starter-level production at a bench price. He's being paid like a star, and the Kings need him to perform like one.

Here's how the rest of the draft unfolded, as managers took shots on late-round sleepers.

A few things stood out. Kristaps Porziņģis (ADP 101.3) went undrafted, likely because he's out indefinitely with an undisclosed illness. Jonathan Kuminga, Bennedict Mathurin and Nikola Vučević went undrafted, too. If we redrafted, I think Kuminga would be drafted late. He looked pretty dynamic in his preseason debut with the Wolves. The others, I expect, will be streaming options who would gain relevancy if an injury occurs.

Round 13 brought the upside swings: rookie Keaton Wagler (who should benefit from Max Strus' foot injury), Ajay Mitchell, Cason Wallace and Kevin Porter Jr. all went. That's how a final round should look. Take your shots on players with higher ceilings if something goes wrong.

As for my last three picks, Aaron Gordon (131) and Draymond Green (134) give me some frontcourt depth after I waited on bigs. I closed with Jimmy Butler III at 155 as a stash. My projections only have him for 36 games, but if he's healthy for the second half, he's a starter in this format. Right now, the belief is Butler should return sometime in early 2027.

articles.title: Conor McGregor’s multi-million philanthropic contributions mark a new milestone as first responder and youth aid tops $5 million
articles.summary: Conor McGregor’s documented charitable giving has crossed the $5 million mark when his major donations and healthcare support are counted.
articles.body: Conor McGregor’s documented charitable giving has crossed the $5 million mark when his major donations and healthcare support are counted. His biggest confirmed contribution is more than $3.7 million from Proper No. Twelve to the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, while a separate $500,000 donation went directly to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Acadiana in Louisiana. In Ireland, McGregor funded more than €1.3 million in protective equipment during the COVID-19 crisis. The money has supported first responders, children, youth programmes and frontline healthcare workers, adding another side to the UFC star’s public profile.How much has Conor McGregor given to first respondersA major part of McGregor’s charitable work has been linked to Proper No. Twelve, the Irish whiskey company he co-founded in 2018.At the time the brand launched, McGregor and his partners pledged to give $5 from every case sold to first responder organisations around the world, with donations capped at $1 million a year.The largest known beneficiary of that plan has been the Tunnel to Towers Foundation, which supports families of fallen first responders and catastrophically injured veterans.The foundation said Proper No. Twelve had given it $3.7 million by March 2022. That included a $1 million donation presented by McGregor to Tunnel to Towers chairman and CEO Frank Siller.McGregor said at the time: “I’m proud of Proper No. Twelve, and all the people working behind the scenes at Proper No. Twelve to make this happen.”He added: “As human beings, it is a must to give back. That’s what life is about, giving back.”The Tunnel to Towers Foundation said the money supports its work with first responder families, including mortgage-free homes for eligible families of fallen first responders and Gold Star families.The foundation has also used donations to support injured veterans and first responders with specially adapted homes.The size of the Proper No. Twelve contribution is important because it was not simply a one-time personal cheque. The donation plan was connected to sales of the whiskey brand, creating a system through which commercial activity could also produce charitable funding.Why did Conor McGregor give $500,000 to Louisiana youthAnother major donation came in April 2021, when McGregor gave $500,000 to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Acadiana in southern Louisiana.The payment came during a public dispute involving McGregor and fellow UFC fighter Dustin Poirier. McGregor had previously pledged $500,000 to Poirier’s Good Fight Foundation, but questions later emerged over how the money would be used.Instead of sending the money through Poirier’s foundation, McGregor sent it directly to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Acadiana.ESPN reported that the donation was intended to support an eight-week summer programme across six club locations. The organisation said more than 600 children would benefit, with the money also supporting health and recreation activities.The club’s then-president and CEO Missy Andrade described the donation as unexpected.“It’s significant,” Andrade said. “It was totally unexpected, of course. Extremely appreciated and it’s really a game-changer for our organization and the kids we have.”The organisation also announced at the time: “This investment is a gamechanger! Thank you, Conor, for helping to ensure that our kids have what they need to grow and thrive this summer!”Poirier later said the decision to send the money directly to the club was not a problem.“Helping people in need was the mission and goal from the jump,” Poirier said.He also added: “It’s not my money – it’s the people’s money.”The donation therefore helped a local youth organisation without passing through Poirier’s charity.What did Conor McGregor donate to Irish hospitalsMcGregor’s healthcare support in Ireland became particularly visible during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.In March that year, he said he would personally buy €1 million worth of protective equipment for medical workers in Leinster, where hospitals were dealing with a serious shortage of supplies.“I have used my platforms multiple times since this has begun. I went further and made the video,” McGregor said.“Today I am purchasing myself, €1 million euro worth of personal protective equipment to be deployed to all the fighting hospitals in the Leinster region.”He then listed several hospitals, including St James’s, the Mater, Tallaght, Beaumont and St Vincent’s.“Our most affected region, to this date. St. James, Mater, Tallaght. Beaumont. Vincent’s. Where would we be without those brave men and women, I do not know. May God bless them and keep them safe!”Reports later put the value of the equipment at more than €1.3 million.The Irish Post reported that the supplies reached hospitals across Ireland, with deliveries including protective masks and other equipment. McGregor and volunteers were also involved in distributing supplies.One update from McGregor’s team said: “28 counties. 165 locations. 18 vans. A real solid day for the team! Tomorrow we go again. Thank you all involved!”He also personally delivered medical supplies to Our Lady’s Children’s Hospital at Crumlin in Dublin during the pandemic.The Irish Independent reported in March 2020 that McGregor had pledged €1 million for protective equipment for frontline healthcare workers. Later reports documented the arrival and distribution of the supplies.How has Conor McGregor supported children and local communitiesMcGregor’s charitable giving has also reached children’s healthcare and smaller community causes in Ireland.In 2023, he donated €10,000 to the Children’s Heart Centre at Our Lady’s Children’s Hospital in Crumlin. The donation was made through a GoFundMe appeal for a child receiving treatment there.That donation was separate from his pandemic PPE effort and showed that his support has also included individual fundraising appeals.There is also a documented example involving SBG Portarlington, a gym connected to McGregor’s longtime coach John Kavanagh. In April 2020, Conor McGregor donated €10,000 to the gym’s “Do It For Dan” fundraiser, according to Laois Today.Other claims about larger grants to boxing and MMA gyms, as well as repeated donations to Crumlin, are harder to establish from reliable public records, so they should not be added to the confirmed total without stronger evidence.Taken together, the better-documented figures show the scale of McGregor’s giving. The more than $3.7 million sent through Proper No. Twelve to Tunnel to Towers, the $500,000 Louisiana youth donation and more than €1.3 million in Irish PPE support alone put his publicly reported contributions well above $5 million when the euro donations are converted to US currency.The figures also show that the money has gone to different groups rather than one single cause. First responder families have received major support through Tunnel to Towers, children and young people have benefited from the Louisiana donation and healthcare workers in Ireland received protective equipment when supplies were difficult to obtain.McGregor’s business success has therefore been tied to several large charitable efforts, with some donations coming directly from him and others through Proper No. Twelve.For a fighter whose career has generated huge pay-per-view numbers and major commercial deals, including the sale of a majority stake in Proper No. Twelve for a deal reported at up to $600 million, the charitable record provides a documented look at where part of that financial success has been directed.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Heisman Rankings: Jeremiah Smith Overtakes Kamario Taylor On RGIII's List
articles.summary: Here are Robert Griffin III's Heisman Trophy front-runners heading into Week 6 of the college football season.
articles.body: Robert Griffin III has a new leader atop his list of Heisman front-runners. After another record-breaking performance, this time against Iowa, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has taken the top spot. And at this point, it’s pretty hard to argue with him. Smith leads a trio of stars at the top of RGIII’s list, with Miami quarterback Darian Mensah and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell right behind him. Mensah continued his dominant season with a statement win over Clemson, while Russell helped Alabama take down Mississippi State. Here are RGIII's top five Heisman Trophy candidates through five weeks of the 2026 college football season. 1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State Griffin's take: "Jeremiah Smith is absolutely balling. He's the best player in the sport right now. What he just did to Iowa was unfair — 11 catches, 206 yards, two touchdowns. But it's really all the records he's breaking, and what he's done in the last five games. His first five games of the year: 44 catches, 823 yards, 18.7 yards per catch, nine touchdowns. He broke the career marks at Ohio State for receptions, receiving touchdowns, yards — 3,381 career yards. I mean back-to-back 200-yard games." 2. Darian Mensah, QB, Miami (FL) Griffin's take: "He might be the first quarterback taken. He has a fight with Jeremiah Smith to be the first overall pick in the draft. Right now, he's playing out of his mind. Darian Mensah is absolutely balling." 3. Keelon Russell, QB, Alabama Griffin's take: "I love what I'm seeing from him because he looks like he's playing free. Every game, he's getting better. His completion percentage is getting better. His ability to take shots down the field is getting better. And he makes Alabama feel like they can be a dominant outfit again. Earlier in the year, everyone was like, ‘What’s it gonna be like with Keelon?' But he hasn't blinked, not one time." 4. Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State Griffin's take: "I know they lost a bad one against Alabama. But he was No. 1 on the list, and from what he's done this year, he's not worthy of falling off that list. He's not healthy. He was not healthy against Alabama. That's not an excuse. It's just a fact. Now he gets a bye week. He gets to come back and, hopefully, he'll be ready to roll, and he can use his arms and his legs to climb back up this list because he's a special player." 5. CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame Griffin's take: "He's been quiet, but Notre Dame is ruthless, man. This guy has completed 71% of his passes, 13 touchdowns, only one interception. I want to continue to see how he grows. Everyone's going to talk about their schedule, but at the end of the day, CJ Carr is balling for what they're asking him to do. And that's why he's at No. 5."

articles.title: How Lionel Messi's $600 million off-field income, hotel stake and $282 million real estate company helped build his $1.1 billion fortune
articles.summary: Forbes now estimates Lionel Messi's net worth at $1.1 billion, which makes him one of only four athletes to reach billionaire status while still playing.
articles.body: Forbes now estimates Lionel Messi's net worth at $1.1 billion, which makes him one of only four athletes to reach billionaire status while still playing. Playing contracts did most of that work, but more than $600 million came from endorsements, memorabilia and business ventures. Messi has also built a portfolio that includes a hotel stake, a listed real estate company and two soccer clubs. The mix explains why his fortune looks built to last, even though a few bets have missed. Here is where the money came from, and which parts are still unproven.How did Messi's off-field income help build his $1.1 billion fortune?It helped, but it was not the whole story, and the numbers show why. Forbes counts about $1.8 billion in career earnings for Messi. Roughly $1.2 billion of that came from playing contracts before taxes and agent fees. The other $600 million came from endorsements, memorabilia and business work. That puts the off-field share at about one third.So the better way to read the headline figure is this. Salary built the base. What he did outside the match decided where that base went next. Forbes says his net worth comes mainly from cash saved over the years, growth in the value of his assets and an option to take a stake in Inter Miami after he retires.Not every outlet lands in the same place. Celebrity Net Worth lists him at $1 billion, $100 million lower than Forbes. Both point the same way, though. Few players in any sport turn playing income into lasting assets, and Messi sits in a short line with LeBron James, Tiger Woods and Cristiano Ronaldo.What does Messi earn each year from endorsements and business deals?About $70 million, according to Forbes. That sits on top of roughly the same amount from the field this season. Add them up and Messi made an estimated $140 million over the past 12 months, third on the 2026 Forbes list of highest-paid athletes. He has not finished lower than fifth since 2014, and he topped the list in 2019 and 2022.Adidas anchors the portfolio. He left Nike for the brand in 2006 and signed a lifetime deal in 2017. Beyond that, he has more than a dozen active partnerships, including Mastercard, Michelob Ultra and Lay's.What stands out is how little he talks. Messi rarely gives interviews, yet brands keep signing him. His late father, Jorge, acted as his agent and business manager, so deals move through a small, steady circle instead of a big public operation. For a sponsor, that kind of calm is hard to find.What is Messi's stake in hotels and the $282 million real estate company?The company is called Edificio Rostower Socimi. Messi launched it in 2024 as a publicly listed real estate investment trust, and it began trading on a small Spanish exchange, the Portfolio Stock Exchange, that December. Forbes puts its market value at $282 million. Celebrity Net Worth cites about $232 million at the time of listing.Inside it sits his stake in MiM Hotels, a boutique chain of six properties across Spain and Andorra. Celebrity Net Worth adds that the company also holds apartments and commercial property.One caution matters here. Neither source says how much of the company Messi personally owns, so the $282 million is not his own wealth. It is better read as a sign of where he is putting money: buildings that earn rent and room revenue.His own homes show the same habit of buying property early and often. He paid about $2 million for a house in Castelldefels, near Barcelona, in 2009. In 2021 he spent $7.3 million on the entire ninth floor of a Sunny Isles Beach condo building. After joining Inter Miami, he bought a Fort Lauderdale waterfront mansion for $10.75 million.Which of Messi's business bets have not paid off?The sports drink is the clearest miss. Más+ by Messi launched in 2024 with Mark Anthony Brands, the company behind White Claw. BevNet reported in May that the brand is being phased out.Other ventures are still running. He is a partner in El Club de la Milanesa, an Argentine restaurant chain. He owns Deportivo LSM in Uruguay, which he founded last year with Inter Miami teammate Luis Suárez, and UE Cornellà, a fifth-tier Spanish club he bought in April for an undisclosed amount. Lower-division clubs rarely pay off fast, so these look like slow plays.The harder lesson on risk came in 2016. A Spanish court found Messi and his father guilty of tax fraud over shell companies in tax havens that held endorsement income. They avoided jail but paid about $4 million in fines. It remains the sharpest reminder that the off-field side of his wealth needs careful handling.How much could Inter Miami add to Messi's wealth?Start with the choice he made. After the 2022 World Cup, Messi could have followed Ronaldo to the Saudi Pro League, where an offer rumored at up to $400 million a year was on the table. He picked Inter Miami and left money behind.What he got in return is more than a salary. The MLS Players Association lists his guaranteed pay at $28.3 million this year, more than double anyone else in the league. Insiders say revenue-sharing deals with MLS partners Adidas and Apple TV add to that. Club owner Jorge Mas told Bloomberg in March that he was paying Messi "$70 million to $80 million a year."The bigger prize is equity. Forbes says Messi secured an option to earn a stake in the club after he retires. Since he arrived, the team's Forbes valuation has climbed from $600 million to $1.35 billion, the highest in MLS. Miami won the 2025 MLS Cup in his second full season, and he signed a three-year extension last October. David Beckham, who laid the blueprint at the club, reached $1 billion 13 years after he retired.No source says how large Messi's stake will be. articles.title: Freddie Freeman Lauds Justin Verlander In Interview After Dodgers' Game 3 Win
articles.summary: Freddie Freeman was caught off-guard by being interviewed by Justin Verlander and in turn praised the future Hall-of-Famer.
articles.body: After the Dodgers' win over the Braves on Tuesday night, a wholesome moment between two future Hall-of-Famers on a night full of stars stole the show. Justin Verlander joined MLB on FOX's coverage of the National League Division Series on Tuesday night, assembling the most accomplished group of analysts ever. There were 50 All-Star appearances on set between Verlander, Alex Rodriguez, David Ortiz, Derek Jeter and Dontrelle Willis. Game 3 of the Dodgers' series against the Braves saw reigning World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto start opposite 10-time All-Star Chris Sale. After Dodgers legend Kike Hernández hit a two-run homer to give L.A. the lead in the third inning, Freddie Freeman hit a solo shot off Sale two batters later. Yamamoto struck out 10 over seven innings of one-run ball to seal the win. After the game, Freeman joined the crew of stars and was surprised when it was Verlander's turn to ask a question. "Hold on, ‘J,’" Freeman said, before reflecting on Verlander's memorable exit during the final start of his career back on Sept. 27. "Congratulations, that was so awesome to watch in that final start. Congratulations on the Hall-of-Fame career. Miss you and congrats." Freeman was referring to the final start of Verlander's career, which saw him throw five innings of two-run ball. The three-time Cy Young Award winner and 2011 American League MVP got the win over the Orioles. It was the moment after the start that will remain in fans' minds forever. As manager A.J. Hinch emerged from the dugout to take Verlander, whom he coached in Houston and Detroit, the right-hander's daughter beat him to the mound. Nine days later, Verlander was in the star-studded studio talking about the MLB postseason. Verlander asked Freeman about facing Sale back in early September, when the Dodgers first baseman notched a base hit against the Braves' southpaw ace. Verlander's question: "Does that give you more confidence going into the game that that happened six weeks ago?" "I mean, just like you, he's going to be in the Hall of Fame," Freeman said. "He's one of the best pitchers in this game. You're just really just trying to hope he makes a mistake, and you're on time for it. Really, it's an extremely hard at-bat for a lefty. "Like I always say, against him, you got to be prepared to die. That's the mindset. If you pull off of him, you got no chance, and he's throwing behind you. So, if he hits you in the ear, you got to be OK with it. So, that's kind of my mentality, and, you know, I was thankfully able to get a good swing on the ball." Before the game, Verlander reflected on his decision to retire, noting that it was clear to him early in the season that it was time. "It was pretty easy," Verlander said. "I made my first start of the season and my leg started hurting. I’ve said my entire career, man, I love this game. I love giving it everything I got. I’m going to play until the wheels fall off. The arm held out great, but the leg gave out on me." Over his 21 seasons in MLB, Verlander built a Hall of Fame resume that includes two World Series titles in addition to his personal accolades. Those honors aren't what he's most proud of, though. "I'm most proud of the volume," said Verlander, who started 557 games in his career, throwing 3,576 2/3 innings while striking out 3,560 batters. "I really pride myself on taking the ball and just being out there for as many pitches as the game would allow. When I look back, I always said that if I’m out there for every start, the numbers fall where they may, but [at least] I’m doing my job."

articles.title: "That’s it, I’m divorcing him"- Former WWE Women's Champion considered ending her marriage
articles.summary: A shocking revelation was made by former WWE Women's Champion, Carmella, who is no longer a part of the company.
articles.body: A shocking revelation was made by former WWE Women's Champion, Carmella, who is no longer a part of the company. She is married to current commentator Corey Graves. However, in a turn of events, the Princess of Staten Island recalled one of the hardest parts of her life that pushed her to the edge, and she actually considered divorcing Graves.What happened that former WWE star Carmella considered ending her marriage?Carmella had gone through an ectopic pregnancy, which was one of the most painful and hardest times of her life. Speaking on her Hot Mom S**t podcast, the former SmackDown Women's Champion revealed that Graves initially did not understand the seriousness of the situation. "I’m in the hospital and I’m getting transported by ambulance to another hospital, and he was just like, ‘Oh, I have to go home,’ because his son was getting a haircut.”Upon hearing that, Mella was left shocked at her husband's behavior in such a serious situation. However, she said that Graves understood all the risks associated with ectopic pregnancy a few days later. Furthermore, Mella also spoke about Graves feeling guilty about not going on a work trip during that time even when WWE had granted him time off. She said, "He was, like, guilty about going to work—I mean, about not going to work. He’s like, ‘Oh, I have to be home with you, but, like, I feel like I should be going to work.’ And I’m like, ‘No, like, you need to be home with me.’”Everything that piled up on Carmella in regards to Corey Graves during her potentially life-threatening pregnancy pushed her so far that the thought of divorcing him actually crossed her mind.“If you’re going to be committed to this relationship, which I—I wasn’t like, ‘That’s it, I’m divorcing him,’ because, I mean, don’t get me wrong, I definitely thought it for a minute. I was like, ‘Does he not even understand that he has to sit with me when I’m sick?’Are Carmella and Corey Graves still together?The couple fought through the difficult situation, and Carmella admitted it made their relationship stronger. On the other hand, while Graves is still a part of WWE, Carmella's contract expired last year amid a hiatus due to pregnancy. articles.title: Messi's Final Match For Argentina Sees The GOAT Score One Last Time
articles.summary: Lionel Messi turns his official farewell match for Argentina into a gala performance, scoring one last time.
articles.body: Lionel Messi turned his official farewell to Argentina into a gala performance, contributing a penalty and two assists in a 3-0 win over Benin in an international friendly on Tuesday at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires, where the crowd offered a deafening final ovation to the genius who, for over two decades, defined the footballing pulse of a nation. In front of 85,000 fans, the superstar capped off an international career spanning 21 years, 126 goals, a 2022 World Cup victory, and two Copa América titles. Orchestrating the win Following a corner kick taken Messi, defender Nicolas Otamendi connected with a header to open the scoring in the 48th minute. Messi then provided an assist to young talent Nicolas Paz, who paid tribute to the star with an exquisite left-foot finish in the 61st. Ten minutes later, Messi buried a left-foot penalty into the top corner, adding to his tally as the Albiceleste’s all-time leading scorer. "Olé, olé, Messi," the crowd chanted in his honor. Passing the torch Despite still playing at a high level at age 39, Messi announced on Aug. 31 that the end of his time with Argentina was set. Messi played his final match — his 208th for Argentina — amid a spectacular fireworks display. He wore a special edition Albiceleste jersey featuring wider vertical stripes than the standard design, a giant sun, and a golden No. 10 on the back. The back detail featured a goat’s horns in the print — a nod to the "GOAT," referencing both the animal and his status as the "Greatest of All Time." Ten minutes after kickoff, the referee paused the match to honor the Argentine captain. Rivals and teammates approached to greet him while fans rose for a standing ovation. Messi raised his hand in acknowledgment. "Come, come, sing with me, and a friend you’ll find; hand in hand with Leo Messi, we’ll all celebrate the victory," the crowd sang to him. From heartbreak to World Cup glory A successor to the legendary Diego Maradona, Messi made his debut for the senior national team in 2005. But his journey was fraught with frustration until 2022, when he finally lifted the World Cup — a triumph that secured his place in the pantheon of the sport’s greatest players and cemented his status as a national hero in Argentina. Accompanied by his sons Thiago, Mateo, and Ciro, Messi was overcome with emotion as the Argentine national anthem played, sung by a veteran of the 1982 Falklands War. Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez tried to comfort him by placing an arm around his shoulders. Devoted fans and moving tributes "It’s not a goodbye, it’s a ‘farewell forever,’ Captain" — that was the message Rebeca Arias and Daniel Lema emblazoned on a hat designed for the occasion. On the brim, they drew various depictions of Messi corresponding to each of the six World Cups he contested. The young couple traveled more than 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from their native Tucumán to witness his final performance. "We believe this is a unique moment. It’s all worth it — being here, making the journey we did. Something like this might never happen again with a player," Arias remarked. In the last World Cup, Messi went close to another title, falling just short after a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the final. However, the runner-up finish didn't overshadow his remarkable performance in the tournament — featuring eight goals and four assists. His contribution was so pivotal that Messi has once again entered the conversation for the Ballon d’Or, competing against the two top contenders to succeed him: Spaniard Lamine Yamal and Frenchman Kylian Mbappé. The Argentine star remains the only footballer to have won the award eight times. Messi receives honorary doctorate Before his farewell at the stadium, Messi received an honorary doctorate from the University of Buenos Aires (UBA), a public institution. The academic institution presented the honor at the national team’s training complex in the suburb of Ezeiza. The star was awarded a diploma and a medal in recognition of his performance with the national team, as well as his influence both on and off the pitch. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: MLB Division Series Roundup: Padres Stay Alive, Dodgers Put Braves On Brink
articles.summary: The Dodgers took control of their NL Division Series on Tuesday night, and the Padres ensured they'll have one more game.
articles.body: The Dodgers took control of their NL Division Series on Tuesday night, and the Padres ensured they'll have one more game – and another chance to rock out to "All The Small Things." In Atlanta, Yoshinobu Yamamoto struck out a postseason career-high 10 in seven innings as Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered in the same inning against Braves ace Chris Sale for a 3-1 Los Angeles win. The Dodgers lead the series 2-1 and are one win from the NLCS in their bid for a third straight World Series title. In San Diego, Jake Cronenworth hit a solo shot and Xander Boegarts scored on a throwing error to help the Padres beat the Brewers 4-3. That means the Brewers, who lead the series 2-1, will try to advance on Wednesday to their second straight NLCS. In the AL, Wednesday brings the ALDS Game 3s, with the White Sox and Rays each up 2-0 and the Guardians and Yankees on the brink. Here is what stood out from Day 4 of the MLB Division Series: Biggest Moment Clutch Run on Error Keeps Padres Alive Every game in the Brewers vs. Padres series has been a nail-biter, and Game 3 in front of a raucous and packed Petco Park in San Diego proved no different. With clutch hits and some beautiful defensive plays, we kind of don't want this series to end. Thankfully, we'll have a Game 4 as the Padres held onto a 4-3 win. In fact, every game in this series has been decided by one run. The deciding moment was a wacky play in the bottom of the sixth inning when baserunner Xander Bogaerts showed off some nifty athleticism by avoiding the barrel of Miguel Andojar's broken-bat grounder. Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt's errant throw to first was bobbled by Jake Bauers, allowing Bogaerts to scoot home. Kudos to Padres pitcher Michael King, as well, who came in the eighth inning in relief to earn his first save since 2023 when he was with the Yankees. He showed some guts in the ninth when he got the Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich to ground out into a double play to secure the win. There will be some sighs of relief across the Gaslamp Quarter tonight as the Padres will try to stave off elimination once again on Wednesday. Best Hitter Kiké Hernández Gives Dodgers a Lift Against Sale Kiké Hernández was the surprise of a lineup Dave Roberts shuffled before first pitch to counter Sale. Making his first start of the playoffs, Hernández came up in the fourth inning after Andy Pages singled and turned on a Sale changeup that stayed up, driving it into the left-field seats for a two-run homer to put the Dodgers ahead. It was his 12th postseason homer as a Dodger and the 17th of his postseason career, and it raised the Dodgers' win probability by nearly 21%. Freeman followed one out later with a solo shot to right, his 18th career postseason homer, for a 3-0 lead. Freeman had been robbed an inning earlier when Mauricio Dubón made a leaping catch at the left-field wall. Sale, who had dominated the Dodgers earlier in the season, was gone after allowing three runs on seven hits in five innings. Hernández has a long record as a postseason hitter, and his homer was the swing that put the Dodgers in position for a series lead. Best Pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto Brings Dodgers One Win From NLCS Yoshinobu Yamamoto made his first postseason appearance since closing out Game 7 of last year's World Series, and he looked like the MVP of that series. He struck out 10 in seven innings, a postseason career high that passed his previous mark of nine in Game 2 of last year's NL Wild Card Series, and he allowed just four hits, one walk and one run. The Dodgers hadn't used him until Game 3, starting lefties Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell against the Braves in Games 1 and 2. The Braves loaded the bases with one out in the fifth and scratched a run across on Drake Baldwin's groundout, but Yamamoto was otherwise in complete control. "I was feeling really good with my fastball," he said. He is the first Dodger with a postseason start of seven-plus innings, 10 strikeouts and one run or fewer since Snell in Game 1 of the 2025 Wild Card, and the third Japanese-born pitcher with double-digit strikeouts in a postseason game, joining Shohei Ohtani and Hiroki Kuroda. He is 8-1 in his postseason career. What's Next The division series continues with the NLDS Game 4 and the ALDS Game 3s on Wednesday. articles.title: Justin Verlander, David Ortiz Put Their MLB Memories To The Test In 'Fact Or Splat'
articles.summary: Can Justin Verlander and David Ortiz remember the biggest moments of their careers?
articles.body: Between the two of them, David Ortiz and Justin Verlander have a combined five World Series rings, 20 All-Star appearances and 3,088 games played in MLB. So, recalling facts about their own illustrious careers shouldn't be too hard for them, right? Their memories were put to the test in a new game called "Fact Or Splat," with some help from Derek Jeter and Alex Rodriguez. The rules are simple: If you get the answer right, you get to drop a fruit on a giant cutout of your opponent's face; if you get it wrong, your opponent gets to drop the fruit. How did Verlander and Big Papi do? Let's see the results: Who did Big Papi hit his first HR off of in Fenway Park? Jeter gave the hint, "It’s someone that’s in the family." Ortiz immediately knew the answer: former Dominican right-hander Ramon Martinez.The cake was a direct hit. Who was Justin Verlander's first strikeout victim? Next, it was Verlander’s turn to answer his first question.Jeter asked, "Who was your first strikeout victim ever in your career?"The recently retired right-hander did not hesitate: "Travis Hafner."It was a fast answer, but Verlander’s toss did not make nearly as impressive contact with Ortiz’s face. Who was Big Papi's longest-tenured teammate? Next up: "Papi, this one’s for you. Who was your longest-tenured teammate?"Ortiz played 20 years in the majors, 14 of which came in Boston. It could have been any number of players.The answer? Dustin Pedroia. Ortiz’s guess was knuckleballer Tim Wakefield.Verlander got better on his second toss and made a direct hit on Ortiz’s face. Which of Jeter, A-Rod and Big Papi had the best batting average against Verlander? Verlander looked around and said, "I’m going to go with Derek." The ace nailed it, and down went a pumpkin onto Big Papi’s face. Who were the three World Series MVPs on Big Papi's title teams? Papi didn’t need much time to answer this one."Manny Ramirez, Mikey Lowell and myself," he answered before cake went falling on Verlander’s face. Which eight of Verlander's teammates have won the Cy Young award? Verlander got Max Scherzer, Rick Porcello, Tarik Skubal (he got a generous hint from A-Rod to get him) and Gerrit Cole. The four players who Verlander missed: Dallas Keuchel, Zack Greinke, David Price and Robbie Ray.

articles.title: Jaguar Type 01: el sorprendente aspecto definitivo de un coche que no se parece a ningún otro
articles.standfirst: Jaguar muestra por primera vez las imágenes definitivas del Type 01, un GT eléctrico de cuatro puertas con hasta 1.030 CV, 720 kilómetros de autonomía y un precio que aproximado de 165.000 euros
articles.summary: Jaguar muestra por primera vez las imágenes definitivas del Type 01, un GT eléctrico de cuatro puertas con hasta 1.030 CV, 720 kilómetros de autonomía y un precio que aproximado de 165.000 euros
articles.body: Jaguar lleva meses hablando de su nueva era, pero hasta ahora no nos había enseñado el Type 01 en su versión definitiva y sin camuflaje. Ya podemos ponerle cara porque la marca ha mostrado al fin las imágenes de su nuevo eléctrico de cuatro puertas, un modelo con el que pretende marcar un punto y aparte en su historia. Por estética, desde luego, va a ser un punto de inflexión. Las imágenes permiten comprobar que aquel prototipo que Jaguar mostró en su primer momento no era solo un ejercicio de diseño. El Type 01 mantiene aquellas proporciones tan extrañas, con el techo bajo, un capó larguísimo y una silueta muy estirada que busca acercarlo más al concepto de un gran turismo de lujo que al de una elegante berlina. Todavía tendremos que esperar al Salón de París para verlo físicamente, pero a juzgar por las imágenes es evidente que será imposible confundirlo con cualquier otro, y eso ya es un valor en una época en la que algunos coches (los SUV asiáticos, sobre todo) se parecen demasiado entre sí. La marca habla de una carrocería creada desde una hoja en blanco y de un diseño que recupera algunos de los rasgos que han definido a sus modelos más reconocibles, con el E-Type y el XJS como principales referencias. El Type 01 es, además, el primer modelo de producción construido sobre la nueva plataforma Jaguar Electric Architecture (JEA), específica para coches eléctricos y responsable de que el 01 pueda lucir unas proporciones diferentes a las de los Jaguar anteriores. Bajo esa carrocería se esconde un sistema capaz de alcanzar los 1.030 CV, aunque la marca todavía no ha detallado todas las características de su sistema de propulsión. Sí sabemos que emplea una arquitectura eléctrica de 850 voltios y que homologa hasta 720 km de autonomía. También que podrá recuperar hasta 320 kilómetros de autonomía en 13 minutos cuando se conecte a un cargador rápido de corriente continua de 350 kW. Son cifras que demuestran que el Type 01 llega con tecnología propia de los coches eléctricos más lujosos, aunque habrá que esperar a conocer sus especificaciones completas y, sobre todo, a conducirlo para comprobar cómo se desenvuelve sobre el asfalto. La propia marca define al Type 01 como el Jaguar de producción más potente y aerodinámico de su historia. Y, puestos a definirlo, su nombre no es fruto del capricho: El 'Type' recupera la denominación utilizada por algunos de los Jaguar más importantes del pasado (ahí está el mítico y bellísimo E-Type, por ejemplo), el '0' hace referencia a las cero emisiones y el '1' identifica al primer modelo de esta nueva generación. Jaguar ha elegido Nueva York para su primera aparición en público sin camuflaje, con una puesta en escena que ha incluido despliegues digitales en Times Square, Dumbo y el Lower East Side, y una presentación en West Chelsea. Allí, por cierto, la actriz británica Florence Pugh ha sido presentada como la primera embajadora de la marca en esta nueva etapa. El Type 01 se fabricará en el Reino Unido y puede que sus oríginales (o extravagantes) líneas sirvan de inspiración a nueva generación de modelos 100% eléctricos por parte de la marca británica. Jaguar asegura que podrá pedirse a comienzos de 2027 y que las primeras entregas están previstas para la segunda mitad de ese año. Eso sí, será muy caro: el precio en España aún no es definitivo pero podría rondar los 165.000 euros.

articles.title: Nike could return to Formula 1 for first time since Michael Schumacher era
articles.summary: Nike has not had a major Formula 1 presence since its Michael Schumacher partnership ended in 2002
articles.body:
It's been a long time since the Nike Swoosh has sat beside the Formula 1 logo. In fact, you'd have to go back to the Michael Schumacher era of the championship to see Nike anywhere near it in a major way. If recent reports are to be believed, this drought could be ending.

The sportswear behemoth recently added a board member with connections to LVMH, the luxury conglomerate that boasts a ten-year partnership with F1 from 2025, and this has knocked over the first domino of speculation. With the championship seeing immense success over the last several years and record growth, Nike could well be seeing potential value hidden within it.

The man in question is Alexandre Arnault. He joined the board of Nike in mid-September earlier this year while also maintaining his role as deputy CEO of Moët Hennessy - the wine and spirits brand under the LVMH umbrella. You'll see Moet in the cooldown room and during the podium after races, but it's Arnault's connection to Nike that is under examination.

The brand's most visible stint in F1 came through Michael Schumacher, who had signed a personal endorsement deal with Nike in 1996 when he moved to Ferrari . It lasted until 2002 before Nike stepped away from any large motorsport sponsorship. But until then, it built the German a shoe that featured red suede, black accents, and a white swoosh.

According to reports, Schumacher loved these kicks and was sent a new pair each race weekend. They're now worth deep into five figures on the used market.

This turned into the Schumacher Collection on its formal launch, with the shoe being named the Nike Air Zoom Schu. They came in three colourways - white, black and blue - and each had a carbon fibre look medallion on the side that featured his signature. Racing versions were also built with them adhering to FIA standards. Unfortunately, in 2002 Ferrari signed with FILA to manufacture shoes for both Schumacher and Rubens Barrichello , and Nike hasn't been seen again in the paddock since apart from occasional, one-off appearances.

According to reports, the iconic brand is looking to supply official teamwear to Formula One Management starting from next year. According to Sports Business Journal, Nike has already been exploring sponsorship and licensing in F1, and executives from the company were even seen at the Miami Grand Prix. The brand has also been connected to Cadillac after its drivers were all spotted wearing Nike shoes. Cadillac F1 CEO Dan Towriss and his wife and chief brand advisor, Cassidy Towriss were also gifted ultra-limited bespoke pair of Dunk Low trainers by the brand itself.

While nothing has been confirmed yet, it's been speculated that we could hear something closer to official around the weekend of the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

This would see Nike join the likes of other fashion houses such as Puma, Adidas, Castore, New Era, Hugo Boss, Tommy Hilfiger, and Gucci.

articles.title: Se rifan a Endrick
articles.standfirst: Las opciones de que el delantero brasileño abandone el Real Madrid en enero están volviendo a crecer
articles.summary: Las opciones de que el delantero brasileño abandone el Real Madrid en enero están volviendo a crecer
articles.body: La vida de Endrick en el Real Madrid no está siendo todo lo armónica que se esperaba cuando el joven delantero aterrizó en la capital de España procedente del Palmeiras por cerca de 50 millones de euros nada más cumplir los 18 años. La competencia en el frente ofensivo continúa siendo feroz y, con el paso de las semanas, las mejores casas de apuestas empiezan a dar credibilidad las opciones de que el brasileño vuelva a salir cedido durante el mercado invernal. Su situación tampoco está ayudando. Una lesión muscular sufrida en mitad de la pretemporada le impidió comenzar el curso con normalidad y, desde entonces, apenas ha podido disfrutar de minutos a las órdenes de Mourinho. De hecho, su única aparición hasta la fecha se produjo frente al Elche, cuando saltó al terreno de juego en el tiempo de descuento. Un escenario complicado para un futbolista que necesita empezar a encontrar cierta continuidad para demostrar todo lo que apuntaba cuando el Real Madrid decidió apostar por él. Además de Vinicius y Mbappé, Endrick parece partir actualmente como el último atacante de la rotación. Diomande, Espí y Brahim han tenido más protagonismo, mientras que Rodrygo se encuentra ya en la recta final de su recuperación y volverá a añadir competencia cuando esté disponible. El brasileño, por tanto, necesita que su situación cambie de forma considerable si quiere disponer de las oportunidades que esperaba encontrar esta temporada. Por ello, la posibilidad de que abandone temporalmente el Real Madrid en enero vuelve a ganar fuerza en las apuestas deportivas. Siempre, bajo la fórmula de una cesión. Betfair, sin embargo, todavía considera que el escenario más probable es que Endrick continúe en el conjunto blanco, con una cuota de 1.67. Entre los clubes que aparecen como posibles destinos destaca, especialmente, el fútbol italiano: la Roma figura con una cuota de 2.88 y el Milan, con 5.5. La Juventus se sitúa algo más lejos, con 13,0, pese a que no ha trascendido ninguna información concreta sobre un interés de los 'bianconeri'. La Premier League también aparece en el horizonte, con el Aston Villa situado en 15.0, mientras que un regreso al Lyon, donde ya estuvo cedido la pasada temporada, alcanza una cuota de 23.0. Novias, desde luego, no le faltan a un Endrick que sigue teniendo claro cuál es su objetivo. Pese a las dificultades que está encontrando para hacerse un hueco, el brasileño quiere triunfar en el Real Madrid y convencer al club de que su futuro pasa por el Santiago Bernabéu.

articles.title: George Russell handed grid penalty for offense ahead of Singapore Grand Prix amid driver's championship competition with teammate Kimi Antonelli
articles.summary: George Russell is set to take a grid penalty at the Singapore Grand Prix 2026 after Mercedes was forced to bring forward a power unit change.
articles.body: George Russell is set to take a grid penalty at the Singapore Grand Prix 2026 after Mercedes was forced to bring forward a power unit change. The decision comes after his late retirement from the Bahrain Grand Prix, where he was on course for a podium finish. The engine failure was another major reliability setback for Mercedes this season.Notably, Russell is already 84 points behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli in the drivers’ championship. The upcoming penalty at the Marina Bay Circuit could make his title challenge even more difficult as the season enters its crucial final stages.George Russell to start from the back in SingaporeGeorge Russell’s engine change was originally expected to happen later in the season. Mercedes had planned to use the FIA’s ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) programme before introducing the updated power unit. However, the damage caused by the failure meant the team had to change its plans.The penalty will apply only to Sunday’s Singapore Grand Prix. It will not affect Saturday’s Sprint. That gives Russell another chance to collect valuable championship points before facing the grid drop in the main race.The Singapore Grand Prix is scheduled to start at 8:00 pm local time on Sunday, October 11. Russell will have a difficult task at the Marina Bay Street Circuit. Overtaking is generally harder on the narrow street track, making a recovery drive from the back particularly challenging.Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff explained that the team is still investigating its recent problems.“Malaysia was obviously a very difficult weekend for us. We have spent the days since then working hard to understand why our performance was not where it should have been. We have identified several areas we need to investigate further, but F1 doesn’t offer simple answers and we need more evidence before drawing firm conclusions”, said Team Principal Toto Wolff in his preview ahead of Singapore.“Singapore gives us an immediate opportunity to continue that work. The characteristics of the circuit are very different and that will help us build a clearer picture of where we are. George has the added challenge of a power unit penalty, which will mean starting from the back of the grid on Sunday, following the engine failure in Malaysia. That is particularly frustrating given the way he drove last weekend and the result he deserved to be fighting for”, he added.The reliability problems have become a major concern for Mercedes in 2026. Russell also retired from the Canadian Grand Prix after a power unit failure. Antonelli suffered a similar issue in Barcelona.Antonelli previously took an engine penalty at the Italian Grand Prix in Monza. Mercedes chose that race because overtaking opportunities made recovery easier. Antonelli started 19th but fought back to win the race.Singapore presents a much tougher challenge. However, Russell won at the Marina Bay Circuit last season. That success could give him confidence as he looks to fight back from the rear of the grid.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Senegal’s AFCON appeal to be heard by CAS after title awarded to Morocco
articles.summary: Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) hearing set to begin after Senegal stripped of Africa Cup of Nations title by CAF.
articles.body:
The long-running saga over the winner of this year’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) title will move closer to resolution on Thursday when Senegal’s appeal, ⁠after being stripped of the title, is heard by the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne.

Senegal are contesting the Confederation of African Football’s decision to declare Morocco champions , despite Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time ⁠in January’s final in Rabat.

Senegal walked off the pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty was awarded against them late in regulation time, with several players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play.

Morocco failed to convert the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal scored the winner to secure victory .

However, they were stripped ‌of the title two months later after CAF’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco.

Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to CAS, which was lodged on March 25 but is only being heard on Thursday . Senegal want to be reinstated as winners, and a panel will listen to arguments from Senegal, Morocco and CAF.

“After the hearing, the panel will start its deliberations. At this stage, CAS cannot state when a final decision will ⁠be rendered but it will not be on the date of the hearing,” CAS ⁠said in a statement.

Three-man CAS panel to hear Senegal and CAF arguments

The panel will be presided over by French civil rights expert Gerald Simon, with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based lawyer and professor of law at the University of Zurich, Ulrich Haas.

They are ⁠likely to hear arguments from Senegal that the Laws of the Game determine the referee’s decisions on incidents of play are final and cannot be challenged after the ⁠fact.

Also important is an interpretation of the articles of the tournament regulations on ⁠which CAF’s Appeals Board ruled in Morocco’s favour, which state that “if, for any reason whatsoever, a team refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered the loser and shall be eliminated for ‌good from the current competition.”

Senegal’s lawyers are expected to argue that the articles must be interpreted strictly and that a temporary departure from the field cannot be equated with abandoning the match, while Morocco are expected to ‌argue ‌for an opposing interpretation, according to which a team that leaves the field without the referee’s authorisation must be considered the loser and definitively eliminated from the competition, even if its departure was not permanent.

The hearing takes place behind closed doors.

Qualification for AFCON 2027 has already begun, with Senegal drawing the opening game of Patrick Vieira’s tenure as coach with Mozambique on September 25, before winning 1-0 in Ethiopia on September 29.

Morocco have won both of their opening games, beating Gabon and Lesotho.
