articles.title: Way-Too-Early Report Card Grades for Every NHL Team After the 1st Week of the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: We are through the first week of the 2026-27 NHL season, and every team has given at least a first impression. Is it an accurate first impression? Maybe. But also... maybe not.
articles.body:
We are through the first week of the 2026-27 NHL season, and every team has given at least a first impression. Is it an accurate first impression? Maybe. But also... maybe not.

The first week of any season can produce some random results, and that will be especially true this season due to the shortened training camp and preseason.

But that doesn't mean we can't still evaluate that first impression and assign a grade based on what it looks like.

This is not a grade on the overall quality of the teams, what is expected of them this season, or where they will be at the end of the season. It is simply a look at what they have done and how they have performed through their first week of the season.

So let's take a way-too-early look at what every team has done so far.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

After a pretty chaotic offseason that saw them use up all of their salary cap space on re-signing their own restricted free agents and not really being able to make improvements to their roster, there was an expectation that the Ducks would take a step backward in 2026-27.

They still might. Especially given the makeup of the defense.

So far? They have played mostly well, jumping out to a 2-0-0 start through Wednesday's games.

Leo Carlsson, their $15 million-per-year man, has been leading the way with five points through two games. They may have had to overpay him after his offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers, but he's the type of player you won't mind overpaying for — a top-line center, just entering the prime of his career, who will only keep getting better for the foreseeable future.

The Bruins will go as far as their top players will take them, and that is especially true when it comes to starting goalie Jeremy Swayman. He had to mask a lot of flaws defensively a year ago, and given the way the roster looks on paper, specifically its defense and the depth in that group, he might have to do it again. So far, he has been up to the challenge with a .914 save percentage through his first three starts.

JJ Peterka has made a nice first impression with two goals in his first four games, while James Hagens is off to a promising start with two goals as well. They are big X-factors this season due to their offensive upside.

After losing Bowen Byram and Alex Tuch over the summer, with nobody else really coming in to replace them, there was some concern over whether or not the Sabres would be hit with some regression this season. That concern isn't gone after three games, but that doesn't take away from the start.

Buffalo has won two of its first three games and, through Wednesday, has mostly pushed the pace, posting a 65.8 expected goals share in 5-on-5 play. That is, as of publication, one week into the season, the highest mark in the league.

Are there concerns about some parts of the roster, and is there a reason to anticipate a small step backward? There are. But they have done a nice job in the first week to at least get things off to a strong start.

Players That Will Dominate the Rumor Mill

This is going to be a very, very long season in Calgary.

This is an extensive rebuild, and it has left the roster with little offensive talent. Their first three games have been completely uncompetitive, with a 16-3 margin of defeat.

Their big offseason move was trading two first-round picks for defenseman Šimon Nemec. It's a fine move and an intriguing addition long-term, but it's not going to be a needle-mover in the short term.

The defending champs are just going about their business, doing their thing by winning the shot-attempt battle, controlling the territorial play, and grinding opponents down. They have recorded at least one point in three of their first four games, despite not having Seth Jarvis in the lineup yet.

There should not be much question about what they are going to be about this season.

The only question is what they do with Alexander Nikishin as a trade chip and how they will use the remaining salary cap space they have to work with. There is still a big move lurking.

Not having Connor Bedard has certainly hurt, but just throwing a bunch of young players to the wolves in the NHL is going to result in a lot of growing pains and probably a lot of bad hockey at times. How much will that impact them, and will it actually lead to real improvement long-term?

Those are big questions with legitimately concerning answers. Some of these games have looked awful early on. They might have a good prospect ranking, but prospects fail more often than not. This is still a bad team facing another long season.

Two games, two wins, two absolute blowouts.

As strong an opening statement as a team can make.

Nathan MacKinnon and Martin Nečas are picking up right where they left off offensively a year ago, while MacKenzie Blackwood has been mostly solid in net.

They lost a lot of depth over the summer, but as long as the superstars are at the top of the lineup and playing the way they are, this is going to be a contender in the West.

The best news for Columbus is that the recently acquired Matthew Knies has made a tremendous first impression with two goals and two assists in his first two games. He may not have the flashy skill that Kirill Marchenko has, but he's a good player, younger than Marchenko, and signed to a better contract. It is a trade that can work out if Knies continues to develop. He is off to a strong start.

At the team level, they played one really solid game and one really awful game, which led head coach Rick Bowness to say they were "exposed."

There is some talent here, but sometimes the vibes around it and the franchise as a whole are alarmingly negative. Bowness is trying to change that. He is going to have his work cut out for him.

This is one of those teams where you shouldn't be overly concerned with or overanalyze early results.

The process has mostly been in place (59 percent expected goal share), the goaltending has been really good, and they have one of their top players, Roope Hintz, back after he missed the end of the 2026-27 season. It's a good team with legitimate Stanley Cup aspirations.

They are 1-2-0 through three games entering play on Wednesday; they could easily be 2-1 given how they played in Game 2 in Nashville.

The organization itself gets an F for the mess it's put itself in with Dylan Larkin, Simon Edvinsson, and the general manager situation. It's created a surreal situation where Larkin is getting booed every time he touches the puck and cheered when he scores (as he did on Tuesday night), while fans fill the space in between by chanting for ownership to sell the team.

The rest of the players and coaching staff are doing what they can under less-than-ideal circumstances. The first two games were ugly, but they did get a nice win against Ottawa on Tuesday night, at least to create some positive momentum.

Offensively, the top guys are off to an incredible start, with Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and Evan Bouchard dominating through the first three games.

Defensively and in goaltending? Still some big concerns there, and they won't go away until they consistently demonstrate improvement in those areas. This season is still going to come down to what the secondary players do to complement McDavid and Draisaitl, and whether or not one of their goalies can make enough saves.

Weird start to the season as Florida has spent most of it either tied or trailing, but is somehow still 2-0-2.

Given the circumstances, opening the season with a four-game road trip that includes the defending Stanley Cup champions, followed by a three-game West Coast swing, that's a solid start, coming away with six out of a possible eight points.

The big concern, however, is going to be injuries.

Aleksander Barkov is out for 6-8 weeks after he missed all of last season.

Then Brad Marchand suffered an ugly injury shortly after he returned to the lineup.

The expectation is that Florida will be significantly better this season and return to being a Stanley Cup contender. Injuries could derail that.

The Kings have settled into a disturbing level of mediocrity over the past few years, and nothing about the roster suggests that will change this season.

It will defend reasonably well. There are a lot of pretty good players who have a role on a playoff team.

But there are simply not enough game-changers here to raise their ceiling beyond what it has been for the past five years (a first-round exit playoff team).

The biggest thing that's hurt them through the first week is that their goaltending is off to a terrible start, with Anton Forsberg and Darcy Kuemper at a combined minus-7.1 in goals saved above expected ( via MoneyPuck ).

I'm not sure that the Wild have really controlled the play in any of their first three games, but they are still 2-0-1, and they will take that.

The biggest factor behind that early success? Starting goalie Jesper Wallstedt has been sensational, posting a .933 all-situations save percentage and 3.1 goals above expected. His name keeps coming up in trade speculation, but it's hard to imagine him going anywhere, especially if he keeps playing like this.

The good news? The offense looks great with 12 goals in three games. Cole Caufield and Nick Suzuki look really good, while Chris Kreider has made a nice early impression, winning over Montreal fans with four points in three games.

The bad news? As good as the 12 goals scored in three games look, the 14 goals against in three games look equally bad.

We know this team can skate, generate offense, and finish. We still need to see a little more from them in terms of slowing other teams down.

It is hard to get a read on what sort of team Nashville is and will be this season. It is even harder to get a read on where they see themselves from a big-picture perspective.

They have an older core that hasn't done much in recent years, and then spent the summer adding depth pieces the way a contending team would. Do they see themselves as a playoff team? Is it one last run with this core to see what happens? It's going to be fascinating to watch play out.

Steven Stamkos and Nils Hoglander (one of those depth additions) are off to strong starts offensively with three goals each.

They haven't really controlled any of their first three games, but they've also played a reasonably tough schedule with Minnesota and Dallas at home and a road game at Toronto.

I am not sure the record or cumulative score accurately reflects how New Jersey has actually played so far.

Offensively, they have scored on just five percent of their shots.

Defensively, they are not getting a save from either goalie.

When it comes to the former, I would imagine that some of those shots are going to start finding the back of the net. Nobody shoots five percent for a full season. There are goals to be had.

When it comes to the latter, it could be a major issue that dramatically changes the season. The goalie duo of Jake Allen and Nico Daws was a big potential red flag coming into the season, and they have done nothing to ease concerns. That position could significantly lower this team's ceiling.

This team was always going to go as far as goalie Ilya Sorokin and defenseman Matthew Schaefer can take them. That is especially true for as long as Mathew Barzal is out.

The good news? A franchise goalie and a No. 1 defenseman can take a team reasonably far, especially when the goalie can reach Sorokin's level, and he has been sensational through his first two starts.

Not just in the sense that they might be competitive again this season, but also in the sense that they are losing the underlying numbers battle in every game but still coming away with wins because their goalie is better than every other goalie and they might have enough finishers to capitalize on the shots they do get.

I wouldn't call this team a contender as far as the Stanley Cup goes, but the playoffs are easily within reach, especially after a strong offseason that saw them add Pavel Dorofeyev, Oliver Bjorkstrand, and Eeli Tolvanen at forward, and also reshape the defense with Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson.

The wild cards are Igor Shesterkin, Adam Fox, and Alexis Lafreniere. Shesterkin and Fox are two of the best at their positions, with both missing significant time a year ago. They are still waiting for the big Lafreniere breakout, and he keeps showing signs and flashes that it can still happen.

Brady Tkachuk is gone, but that shouldn't make you write them off just yet.

The defensive structure that made them a playoff team over the past two seasons is still there, and it is reasonable to expect a bounce-back season from Linus Ullmark in goal. If they can, the playoffs are within reach.

There is still a good core here, and now they don't have to deal with the uncertainty of whether their captain wants to be there or listen to his family critique his usage and ice time on a podcast.

Not just in terms of the results, but also in the process behind those results. They are not just losing games; they are getting completely and thoroughly dominated. Outside of signing Leo Carlsson to the restricted free-agent offer sheet (and then watching Anaheim match it), they didn't really do much to change the roster and were largely banking on internal improvement from their young players.

It is still early, and there is still plenty of time for that to happen.

But through the first week, this looks like a team that did nothing to its roster and heard its general manager tell the public there was a good chance they would take a step backward this season, and that they were ready for it. Not exactly what you want to hear after reaching the second round of the playoffs. This also is not the type of hockey you want to see after that.

There is a ton of forward depth here, and that has mostly been on display. Ben Kindel, their second-year center in his age-19 season, has looked like their best player so far, which is a great sign given how important he will be for them long-term.

They still have some issues they need to clean up on their own end.

They will score goals, and they will score a lot of them. Their ability to hold on to leads and get solid goaltending from Artūrs Šilovs and Sergei Murashov will determine how good their season can be. Both goalies have made strong first impressions despite some shoddy defensive work in front of them at times.

So far, the Sharks have been exactly what their roster says they will be. When things are going well, they will have a potentially electrifying offense, with Macklin Celebrini leading the way.

They are also going to struggle defensively and to consistently push the pace of the game.

They have allowed 12 goals in three games and have a 29 percent expected goal share. That's a problem. Also a problem: Celebrini is currently dealing with a lower-body injury, and in the game he missed, they lost 5-0 and were not even competitive.

Exciting team. A lot of long-term potential.

But an exciting team that still has many flaws and a long way to go before it realizes all its potential.

The one thing we can definitively say about the 2026-27 Seattle Kraken: They are significantly better than the Calgary Flames, beating them in two games by a combined score of 12-2.

They are 0-2 and have been outscored 9-3 by teams other than the Calgary Flames.

In some ways, this start is the absolute perfect representation of what the Kraken are as an organization. They are better than the absolute worst teams in the league and not quite stuck in that pit of losing. But they are also nowhere near as good as the top teams and are not really climbing that mountain to catch up to them.

They haven't really received anything offensive from Robert Thomas, Jake Neighbours, or Pavel Buchnevich yet. That will change, and when it does, it will help a lot. They are too good to be this quiet for long.

They have received one start from Jordan Binnington, and he allowed six goals and looked like a one-man self-destruction wrecking crew. The point here is that Joel Hofer is this team's best goalie, and he needs to be utilized as he is.

Tough game to open the season against the Rangers, but a nice response in the next two games, completely dominating Washington and Philadelphia. They have a 62 percent expected goals share through three games (third-best in the league) and are mostly dominating play in 5-on-5 situations.

It is a good team, even if playoff success hasn't been there in recent years. There are still some things to fix from a depth perspective, but the guys at the top of the lineup (Nikita Kucherov, Jake Guentzel, Brayden Point, Andrei Vasilevskiy) still have a lot to give.

The Maple Leafs should be highly encouraged by what they are seeing from Auston Matthews and William Nylander so far.

They should have some minor concern over what Sergei Bobrovsky has done so far and their overall defensive play.

Bobrovsky is one of the big-ticket offseason moves, and the one most likely to impact things given his position. He was awful in Florida a year ago and is a year older now. Is he a Hall of Famer? Yes. Has he won a lot? Also yes. Is he going to win the fight with Father Time? Nobody ever does.

Utah has not yet played the most daunting schedule in terms of opponents, but sometimes a sign of a good team is simply taking care of business against lesser teams and soundly beating them.

The Mammoth enter play on Wednesday having won three of their first four games, scoring 17 goals and winning each by multiple goals.

Utah was a playoff team a year ago, and after adding Vincent Trocheck and Anders Lee this summer, there is a real reason to believe they can be a contender. Especially if they can get even average goaltending.

Are we grading on a curve here with the Canucks? Sure. This team was supposed to be awful, and it will still probably end up as one of the worst teams in the league. But winning two of their first four games and then losing a one-goal game to Vegas is a strong start and a strong effort.

Elias Pettersson with six points in four games and Marco Rossi already scoring three goals are also very encouraging developments.

Whether they are contending this season or not, they need those two guys to be good and produce. Strong start for both of them.

Remember what we said up above about Utah and good teams soundly beating the teams they should beat?

On an individual level, forward Jack Eichel is cooking everybody with 10 points in four games as he looks poised for his third consecutive 90-point season. Perhaps even his first 100-point season.

The Capitals absolutely dominated Carolina in their season-opener and then lost a tough game against Tampa Bay in their second game.

Expectations are extremely high here for this season, and they should be given the depth of the roster on paper and the offseason they had. It is also officially Alex Ovechkin's retirement season, and there is going to be a lot of incentive to send him into retirement on top. They have the roster that can do that. Or at least compete for it.

Alex Tuch, one of their biggest offseason additions, made a strong first impression with two goals in his debut game with the team.

They lack a superstar at the top of the lineup (Ovechkin is still a big name, but he is no longer a superstar in terms of impact), but the depth here is so overwhelming that there is no real weakness anywhere on the roster.

The Connor Hellebuyck situation is not great, and his absence and eventual departure could be a problem this season. It still seems like an organization that is stuck in neutral under the current management and ownership. But it is hard to complain about the start of the season with five out of a possible six points in three games.

Kyle Connor is off to another great start offensively, while Clay Stevenson had an outstanding debut in his first start. He is an intriguing goalie given his minor league success and is going to get a real opportunity here.

articles.title: Canadiens, Jets Unveil NHL Heritage Classic Uniforms in New Photos Ahead of Outdoor Game
articles.summary: The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets are bringing vintage looks to the 2026 Heritage Classic.
articles.body:
The Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets are bringing vintage looks to the 2026 Heritage Classic.

The Canadiens and Jets revealed a first look Wednesday at the uniforms that will be worn during their upcoming outdoor game at Winnipeg's Princess Auto Stadium.

Players That Will Dominate the Rumor Mill

The puck will drop for the 2026 Heritage Classic Sunday, Oct. 25 at 7 p.m. ET.

The Canadiens uniform features a redrawn "CH" crest made of felt as well as off-white stripes inspired by the franchise's vintage uniforms, according to the NHL .

The jerseys also feature the club's nickname of "Les Habitants" stitched for the first time in franchise history inside the back collar, per the league. The loop label also features a fleur-de-lis in honor of Québec.

The Jets are using a similar crest to the one featured on the team's current navy blue alternate uniforms.

This version of the crest, which is felted and on a white jersey, is designed in honor of the logo the team wore during its original iteration from 1979 before relocating to Phoenix in 1996.

Players have regularly worn the team's current military-inspired fighter jet logo since the Atlanta Thrashers returned to Winnipeg in 2011.

This marks the third time the Jets have played an outdoor game , and the first since their 2019 Heritage Classic matchup against the Calgary Flames in Regina.

The Canadiens are heading into their fifth outdoor matchup and their first since playing the 2017 NHL100 Classic against the Ottawa Senators in Ottawa.

The NHL first debuted the Heritage Classic with a 2003 matchup between the Canadiens and Edmonton Oilers at Commonwealth Stadium in Edmonton. Temperatures that day were around zero degrees Fahrenheit, according to the league .

The Habs and Jets will be expected more moderate temperatures when playing later this month at the home of the CFL's Winnipeg Blue Bombers. The Weather Channel predicts an average temperature of around 46 degrees on game day in Winnipeg.

articles.title: Luke Littler: World champion can still qualify for Players Championship Finals – but will he play, and what else can he win?
articles.summary: What's next for Luke Littler? Can he still qualify for the Players Championship Finals and what else can he win this season? you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
His unprecedented 12-month clean sweep may be over following a crushing 10-4 defeat by Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam and a shock first-round exit at the World Grand Prix , but he can still qualify for next month's Players Championship Finals.

The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

He had been hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic clean sweep of the year. But his bid was derailed by Clayton, who reeled off seven of the final eight legs to defeat the teenager before overcoming Luke Woodhouse in Leicester, where he suffered a 2-1 defeat in the double-in, double-out tournament.

Had he gone on to win the title, Littler would have become the first player to hold both the World Championship and World Youth titles.

The final will take place on Sunday, November 29, in Minehead as part of the Players Championship Finals, a tournament Littler won last year but has yet to qualify for this time around.

With just two floor events remaining before the Players Championship Finals, Littler can still earn enough prize money to qualify for the tournament - but will he make the trip to Leicester on November 4 and 5?

The top 64 players on the ProTour Order of Merit qualify for the Minehead showpiece, with the projected cut-off expected to exceed £30,000 after all 34 events. Littler currently sits in 126th place with £10,500, while Mike De Decker occupies the final qualifying spot in 64th with £29,250.

That leaves 'The Nuke' with a slim route into Minehead, but he would likely need to reach the final of at least one - and potentially both - of the final two ProTour events to force his way into the field.

Littler won the 2025 title, defeating Nathan Aspinall 11-8 in the final.

Speaking on the Love The Darts podcast, Matt Edgar believes Littler is unlikely to compete in the final two ProTour events of the season

"There is an opportunity here to be undisputed champion of the world - to own both of those world championships in the PDC. Playing in the World Youth Championship was an interesting decision. I didn't think he would make it, but I'm kind of glad he did," said Edgar.

"I also think there's a big misunderstanding about what that tournament was because there were people suggesting that maybe he shouldn't have been there. This isn't the Development Tour Finals. This was a world championship, and I don't ever want to exist in a world of sport where someone is excluded from a world championship for being too good.

"I'm glad he went to the World Youth Championship, but I think if he had got to the final, then maybe we would have seen him at the ProTours. There's no point going all the way down to Minehead if you're not going to play the Players Championship Finals as well.

"I think he would [have played the final two ProTour events] had he got into the World Youth final, but I think now it's off the cards."

You would be brave to bet against Luke Littler winning the Grand Slam of Darts because the Warrington phenom has a perfect career record at the tournament in Wolverhampton, backing up his 2024 triumph with victory last year.

And then to Alexandra Palace where the teenager will bid to become a triple world champion.

He is aiming to become the first player to win three world titles in a row since Phil Taylor did it in 2006, although 'The Power' did win eight in a row from 1995 to 2002.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Junior Caminero would be a household name if he was in the Bronx. Instead, he’ll look to end the Yankees’ season there
articles.summary: If he played in New York, Junior Caminero would be the next big thing. Instead, he’s aiming to take down the powerful Yankees this week.
articles.body: Chad Mottola, the hitting coach for the Tampa Bay Rays for the past decade, sat in the visiting team dugout alongside speedy slap-hitter Chandler Simpson and budding star Junior Caminero, who was nearing the end of his first full season in the majors. It was late September 2025. Caminero’s baseball year had started with a bang back in January, when the then-21-year-old hit a ball 454 feet to clinch a championship in the Dominican Winter League. Even in a nation known for ostentatious displays of baseball obsession, the ensuing theatrics went viral. Stateside for the Rays, the young slugger had hit 45 home runs, been an All-Star, and competed in the Home Run Derby. But now, he was watching the Toronto Blue Jays celebrate having clinched the division on the last day of the season. The Blue Jays were about to go on a magical run that would come within inches of a title, ultimately falling short in an all-time classic of a World Series. Caminero’s Rays, on the other hand, were headed home. Already, the rest of the team had descended to the clubhouse to start their offseason. Mottola, Simpson, and Caminero lingered and let the bad feeling of watching someone else revel in success to sink in. Mottola turned to his young players. “That’s us next year,” he said. And it was. The Rays clinched the 2026 American League East with a victory over the New York Yankees in the Bronx, the most famous franchise in the sport relegated to a wild card berth. The team with the third-lowest payroll in Major League Baseball had toppled the team with the third-highest payroll, on that night and in the division. “Amazing, amazing,” Caminero told CNN Sports, recalling the celebration two days later. “But we gotta continue. We need the American (League). We need the World Series.” He spoke in English. Caminero is from Santo Domingo, capital of the Dominican Republic. His love for baseball is both cultural – the DR sends more players to the majors than any other country outside the United States – and personal. Caminero is one of those players who, even amid a 162-game season, spends his off days watching baseball. Despite it being his second language, and the prevalence of Spanish in the big leagues, Caminero has started doing more interviews in English. In July, he appeared on Jeff Passan’s podcast at ESPN for an hour, all in English. Caminero was forthright and far-ranging, talking about the trade that brought him to the Rays as a minor leaguer as well as why Latin players aren’t more involved in the Players Association. He was also funny, poking fun at his own plodding speed on the basepaths and demonstrating his best Australian accent. It’s a personality and a propensity to be known that could make him one of baseball’s rare breakout stars – combined, of course, with the performance. Caminero boasts the fastest bat speed in the majors. Over the past two seasons combined, he has the second-most home runs in baseball, the most in the American League. More than global sensation and four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani. More than three-time MVP and Yankees captain Aaron Judge, who was sidelined with injury for most of this year. More than Ben Rice, who has stepped up in Judge’s absence to be the preeminent Bomber in the Bronx. “He has a high ceiling, but he also has aptitude,” said Mottola, who credits Caminero with reinvigorating his own enthusiasm for the game. Caminero’s willingness to work, to make mistakes, to learn and improve – he nearly doubled his walk rate year over year – is rare for someone so talented. “I don’t know if I’ve ever had a teammate or a player that can do the things he does,” Mottola said. “He has every attribute that you would consider a star player to have,” Rays shortstop Taylor Walls told CNN Sports. “I guess the market being smaller, you may not hear about him quite as much as you would hear about other bigger-market names, but based on just pure performance and play, 100%.” Walls is correct. You don’t hear about Caminero as much as his output merits because of where he plays. The Rays are a scrappy organization. Perennial contenders despite the payroll constraints, unbothered by their underdog status even after clinching the top seed in the league. Historically, the team has succeeded by being greater than the sum of its parts. Neither stars nor scrubs but rather an optimized collection of skills buoyed by collective buy-in. There have only ever been seven seasons of more than 35 home runs authored by Rays players and already, at 23 years old, Caminero is responsible for two of them. If he played in New York, Caminero would be the next big thing. The kid who convinced his parents to name his little brother after former Yankees manager Joe Girardi now an unstoppable slugger? That’s superstar material. In pinstripes, Caminero would have been a Yankee hero. Instead, he’ll look to end their season. Two weeks after the Rays clinched the division in New York, they return to the Bronx on Wednesday with a commanding 2-0 lead in the division series over the Yankees. History says they have a nearly 90% chance of advancing to the championship series. They have two shots at a dogpile celebration in front of a hostile crowd. Despite winning the division, given the disparity in market, payroll, and legacy – the Rays have two pennants, but no World Series titles, in their 29-year history – it would still be seen as David taking down Goliath. “The national media always paints a picture that we’re overperforming,” Mottola said. “We have really good players that don’t get the attention they should. And rightly so, probably during the playoff time, the way (Caminero) is, his personality will probably get a lot more attention.” That way is respectful – of the veterans in the clubhouse and the game that he still hasn’t fully mastered. “I try to stay more humble,” Caminero said. But not shrinking. “I know who I am,” he said. “He likes the adrenaline,” Mottola said, “He likes to feel like, OK, something special is going to happen.” And if this October he rises to those occasions when the stakes are the highest, would that make him transcend the market to join the ranks of baseball stars? “Wallsy, tell ‘em,” Caminero deflected when asked directly. “He is a superstar,” Walls said.

articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling.

Where Things Reportedly Stand Between Sheamus, AEW

Why Your Favorite Star Will Lose MITB Ladder Matches 😔

Despite interest, AEW reportedly hasn't made a significant push to sign longtime WWE Superstar Sheamus in free agency yet.

According to Fightful Wrestling , some "big veteran names" within AEW have pushed for the company to sign Sheamus, but there have not been any "substantial talks" between the two sides to this point.

It was initially reported in July by Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats) that Sheamus would be departing WWE at the expiration of his contract after rejecting an offer by WWE to restructure his deal.

More recently, Fightful Select (h/t Fightful's Ishaan Sharma ) reported that The Celtic Warrior officially became a free agent on Oct. 1.

That means Sheamus is clear to negotiate a contract with any company, including AEW.

The reported internal push to sign Sheamus in AEW doesn't come as a huge surprise since many key members on the roster worked with him previously in WWE, including Claudio Castagnoli, The New Level, Jon Moxley and a host of others.

Although Sheamus is 48 years of age, he looked to have plenty left in the tank when he was last seen in the ring last year.

On top of that, his résumé speaks for itself as a multi-time world champion, and he would undoubtedly bring additional credibility to the AEW roster.

WWE's Reported View on Enzo and Cass Reunion

Despite their success as a tag team once upon a time, WWE reportedly did not originally have designs on reuniting Big Cass and Enzo Amore.

According to Dave Meltzer of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), he heard talk of Enzo's return being a "done deal" at one point, but the working idea was that he and Cass would be kept separated.

Meltzer mentioned NXT as a potential destination for Enzo, whereas Cass has been part of the Raw roster since his return in August.

Per Meltzer, the idea of keeping Enzo and Cass apart had to do with WWE not wanting to limit Cass' upside, but now with Cass losing singles matches recently, he theorized that an Enzo and Cass reunion could be possible.

Cass' WWE return saw him target Je'Von Evans with attacks before beating Evans in his return match on the Aug. 24 episode of Raw.

However, Evans later beat Cass and Austin Theory in a Money in the Bank qualifying match on Sept. 21, and one week later, Cass surprisingly lost a singles bout to Dragon Lee via rollup.

This week on Raw, Cass got some revenge by attacking Lee and his tag team partner, Rey Mysterio, leading to speculation that Enzo could possibly return and join forces with Cass as part of a tag team rivalry.

While it remains to be seen if that is actually the direction WWE is moving in, there is no question that Enzo and Cass were a hugely entertaining pairing in the past.

They were among the most popular acts in NXT, and although they didn't stay together long after getting called up to WWE's main roster in 2016, they were over with the fans during that stint as well.

It is fair to wonder how Enzo and Cass would work as a heel tandem rather than babyfaces, but it may be worth it for WWE to explore it.

Latest on 2027 Elimination Chamber Location

The Elimination Chamber premium live event has often been held outside the United States in recent years, but that reportedly may not be the case when it comes to the 2027 edition.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), rumors suggest Elimination Chamber 2027 will take place in the U.S.

Elimination Chamber 2026 represented the show's return to the United States, as the previous four versions of the show were international.

In 2022, Elimination Chamber was in Saudi Arabia, followed by Montreal in 2023, Australia in 2024 and Toronto in 2025.

Given that it occurs on the road to WrestleMania, some hugely newsworthy things have happened at Elimination Chamber over the past few years, including John Cena's shocking heel turn in 2025.

Regardless of where it is hosted, Elimination Chamber figures to be a massive show once again in 2027, as it will likely determine the challengers for two major championships at WrestleMania 43 based on who wins the men's and women's Elimination Chamber matches.

articles.title: Texans HC DeMeco Ryans on defense's struggles with explosive plays
articles.summary: Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans addresses the Texans' struggles on defense allowing explosive plays.
articles.body:
The Houston Texans had one of the best defensive units in the NFL entering 2026.

That still could be true, but it's been anything but top-notch amid an 0-4 start. Houston still has the talent to have one of the league's defenses, but that is not happening so far this season, particularly in the season opener against the Buffalo Bills and the Week 4 loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Against Dallas, Houston had a problem preventing explosive plays. Pro Bowl receiver George Pickens had a 53-yard reception while All-Pro CeeDee Lamb's longest reception was 30 yards. Even if it was just outside the reach of what fan list as explosives, Lamb had a career-high 17 receptions and couldn't be stopped.

Two running backs for Dallas had runs of over 10 yards and its top back, Javonte Williams, scored three touchdowns. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans addressed the defense's inability to limit explosive plays so far this year.

"For me, it comes down to being where you're supposed to be, playing technique the proper way on defense. That's what it all comes down to," Ryans said. "A couple times we drop coverage, just poor execution by us defensively, not doing the coverage the proper way."

With a winless record, the Texans have already dug themselves in a hole that is nearly impossible to come out of. If they are going to have any chance of making the playoffs, they need to win their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans .

The Titans are not known for their explosive offense and have not scored a lot of points this season, with their most points in a game coming in their Week 2 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at home. Houston also hasn't lost at Nissan Stadium since the 2020 season, with the most points being scored set at 16.

articles.title: Oregon MBB tabs Tony Stubblefield as interim coach after Dana Altman's retirement
articles.summary: Following Dana Altman's shocking retirement, Tony Stubblefield will lead the Ducks into the season as the interim head coach.
articles.body:
It's a new era in Eugene for Oregon Ducks men's basketball, as Dana Altman stunningly announced his retirement just before the 2026-27 season is set to begin. The Ducks overhauled the roster in Eugene this offseason, largely thanks to Altman's efforts, but now someone else will lead the group into the season.

That someone happens to be assistant coach Tony Stubblefield , who will serve as the interim coach for the year, according to ESPN's Pete Thamel. Stubblefield has been a big part of Oregon's recruiting success over the years and is a longtime assistant alongside Altman.

Stubblefield spent four seasons as a recruiting coordinator at Cincinnati and six seasons as an assistant coach at New Mexico State before joining Oregon's staff in 2010. He helped reel in some of the top national recruiting classes at Oregon, which included players such as Payton Pritchard , Troy Brown Jr. and Bol Bol.

Stubblefield left Eugene to become the head coach at DePaul in 2021 before he was let go in 2024. He finished with a 28-54 record over three seasons with the Blue Demons. He rejoined Altman's staff with the Ducks before the 2024 season and returned to his role on the bench. The Ducks reached eight NCAA Tournaments, including five Sweet 16s, two Elite Eights, and a Final Four with Stubblefield on staff.

Oregon is experiencing a change just before the season that very few saw coming. Stubblefield is held in high regard both inside and outside of the program, but he is facing a massive task to take over the reins from Altman and hopefully keep members of the Ducks' new roster from transferring before the season begins.

articles.title: Lion Tales: USC
articles.summary: USC will make the journey to Beaver Stadium for the first time in more than 30 years on Saturday night for the annual White Out. Today’s Lion Tales goes back...
articles.body:
USC will make the journey to Beaver Stadium for the first time in more than 30 years on Saturday night for the annual White Out.

Today's Lion Tales goes back to that trip – September 10, 1994.

One can never write or think about that 1994 team too often, but a little context headed into that Saturday afternoon.

The Nittany Lions were ranked No. 8 coming off a season-opening rout of Minnesota at the Metrodome. Meanwhile, USC had earned a ranked win it its opener, outlasting Washington at the Memorial Coliseum.

The Trojans were ranked No. 14 and were led by quarterback Rob Johnson, viewed by some as a Heisman contender.

His early gaffe paved the way for Penn State's explosive offense to put this one soon after it started. Penn State marched for an early scoring drive, capped by Ki-Jana Carter racing to give the Lions the 7-0 lead. Johnson fumbled a snap on USC's first drive. Offensive coordinator Fran Ganter went right for the kill, calling a deep pass down the right sideline from Kerry Collins to Freddie Scott.

The junior wide receiver made an acrobatic catch, Penn State led 14-0 with 12:55 to go in the first quarter and USC coach John Robinson knew his team was in trouble.

Penn State added another score in the first quarter and two more in the second to lead 35-0 at the break. Carter finished with 119 yards rushing, 67 of those in the first quarter. For the game, Penn State ran for nearly 300 yards.

USC's first score came on a rare Kerry Collins mistake. He had an interception returned for a touchdown as the Trojans made things look a little closer by outscoring the Penn State backups 14-3 in the second half.

Meanwhile, it should be noted that Penn State's sometimes maligned 1994 defense sacked Johnson six times and came away with the turnover. USC was playing without top wide receiver Keyshawn Johnson, but Rob Johnson completed just 18-of-30 passes for 221 yards.

The Penn State win completed a four-year home-and-home series with the Trojans. Penn State and USC had played just twice before that four year stretch of 1990-1994. USC won both games in the Coliseum, including a 1991 win against a Penn State that wound up No. 3 in the country. Meanwhile, the Lions had snuck out a win early in 1993 at Beaver Stadium before the shellacking that happened in September 1994.

The Nittany Lions famously wound up going 12-0, but being uncrowned despite their prolific offense and mostly running roughshod through the Big Ten. In one of those weird 2026 anomalies, 11 of Penn State's 12 games were played against teams that are currently in the Big Ten.

The Trojans didn't miss out on a rematch with Penn State in Pasadena by much. A late season loss at UCLA cost USC a share of the Pac 10 title. However, Oregon would still have won the tiebreak. So, it was the Ducks who were dominated in the latter half of that year's Rose Bowl by the Lions.

Meanwhile, USC wound up finishing 8-3-1 and they were ranked No. 13 in the season's final AP poll. They dominated Texas Tech in the Cotton Bowl. A year later, behind the efforts of Keyshawn Johnson, they would win the Rose Bowl over upstart Northwestern.

articles.title: Tropical storm may force Mississippi football schedule changes
articles.summary: Mississippi high school football games may move to Thursday as Tropical Storm Isaias threatens the Gulf Coast.
articles.body:
High school football programs in Mississippi are preparing for possible schedule changes later this week as a tropical system in the Gulf of Mexico threatens to bring heavy rain, strong winds and flooding to parts of the state.

The National Hurricane Center has issued hurricane and tropical storm watches affecting portions of Mississippi as Tropical Storm Isaias moves toward the northern Gulf Coast. Forecasters said Mississippi faces a risk of heavy rainfall, flooding and gusty winds as the storm approaches.

With weather conditions expected to worsen around the end of the week, representatives of both the Mississippi High School Activities Association and the Mid-South Association of Independent Schools told the Clarion Ledger that school administrators and athletic officials are monitoring forecasts and discussing whether games scheduled for Friday night should be moved earlier in the week, likely Thursday.

Similar weather threats last week prompted widespread schedule adjustments in Mississippi high school football, with many MHSAA and MAIS games moved from Friday to Thursday.

Moving games ahead of the storm would allow teams to avoid lightning, flooding and hazardous travel conditions that often accompany tropical weather systems.

The MHSAA has not announced statewide schedule changes, but schools are expected to make decisions based on local forecasts and guidance from district administrators.

articles.body:
March Madness: Men's college basketball national champions since 1960

Oregon men's basketball coach Dana Altman is retiring, USA TODAY Sports has confirmed: a stunning move, particularly since it takes place less than one month before the 2026-27 season begins.

Longtime assistant coach and former DePaul coach Tony Stubblefield will serve as the interim coach for the upcoming season, USA TODAY Sports also confirmed.

The winningest coach in program history, Altman has been at Oregon since 2010. He made the Ducks a consistent contender during his 16 seasons in Eugene, winning four Pac-12 Tournament titles and leading the team to nine NCAA tournament berths, including the 2017 Final Four that was the program's first appearance in 78 years.

However, Altman is coming off his worst season of his tenure. Injuries and inconsistent play led to a 12–20 record and a 5-15 mark in the Big Ten that resulted in a 15th-place finish, the first time Oregon had finished worse than eighth in its conference.

There was massive turnover on Oregon's roster going into the 2026-7 season, as well.

The timing of the decision is notable, considering the preparation for the 2026-27 season is in full swing. Oregon is set to participate in Big Ten media days on Thursday, Oct. 8, and its first scrimmage is scheduled against Seattle on Oct. 15. The Ducks officially kick off the season on Nov. 2 against Montana.

Altman finishes with a record of 382-182 with Oregon.

articles.title: Kevin Keegan, Gordon McKeag, Tony Cunningham, Newcastle United heroes and villains
articles.summary: Here at The Mag we invited a number of regular/irregular contributors to give us their Newcastle United heroes and villains. Our thanks to ‘Matt Busby said t...
articles.body:
Here at The Mag we invited a number of regular/irregular contributors to give us their Newcastle United heroes and villains.

Our thanks to 'Matt Busby said to Joe Harvey' for taking up the challenge.

He has looked back at his Newcastle United heroes and villains across the various decades when he has been supporting NUFC.

My hero of the 1980s was undoubtedly King Kev, the great man sadly passing away in the summer, the floral carpet outside St James' Park placed in tribute and then the Wor Flags display before the Liverpool game.

Of course, Kevin Keegan also managed Newcastle United, not once but twice in the decades that followed, but his time spent playing in the black and white stripes in the two years between 1982 and 1984 left an indelible mark on everyone that bore witness to this incredibly special period. I'd seen nothing like the scenes in and around St James' Park when Keegan scored on his debut against QPR and by the time he left us, he'd got back us to the big time, promoted in third place from the old Second Division in May 1984 and before the need for play-offs. The trips to Maine Road, Ewood Park and Leeds Road in that incredible run in will stay with me forever.

As for my villain of that decade, it has to be Gordon McKeag.

A club director, McKeag became chairman in 1988 and presided over a miserable relegation to the second tier, while St. James Park suffered from later low crowds and a severe lack of modernisation.

To fans, McKeag was the face of an outdated board that refused to invest in the first team and with "Sack the Board" chants, the atmosphere at home matches grew more and more hostile. The narrative of McKeag as villain was amplified by the arrival of Sir John Hall and the Magpie Group, with McKeag using his legal expertise to try and block Hall. Most fans resented that stubborn resistance, with McKeag and his acolytes seen as a symbol of an archaic footballing oligarchy.

When it comes to a cult hero of the 1980s…

When I began to regularly attending Newcastle United matches in the 1980s, Tyneside was gripped by industrial decline, the football club was trapped in a seemingly endless cycle of crises, and the terraces at St James' Park were a radically different, far more volatile environment than the stadium we know today.

It was against this backdrop that in 1985, a quiet piece of history was made.

When Tony Cunningham signed on the dotted line for Newcastle United in February 1985, he wasn't just inheriting a shirt. By stepping out onto a snow-covered pitch against Man U for his debut, the Jamaican-born striker became the first black player in United's history to be signed on a permanent contract.

Big Tony's time on Tyneside needs to be seen in the context of the ugly reality of the era.

Football in the 1980s was plagued by systemic racism, and St James' Park was no exception. Sadly, I can still recall copies of the National Front publication, Bulldog being sold outside the ground. And like all black players of that era, Cunningham had to endure such prejudice from his own fans just as much as the abuse that came from fans of opposing teams.

It was Jack Charlton who bought the 6ft 2in frontman from Manchester City .

Big Jack wanted a physical, uncompromising target man and in Cunningham, what he got was someone who maybe did more to bring others into the game, as opposed to stealing the limelight himself.

I think that judging Cunningham solely on his goal return (6 goals in 51 appearances) somewhat makes my point. He was a battering ram. He chased lost causes, put his head where boots were flying, and gave absolutely everything for the black and white stripes.

On a sunny day in Nottingham in May 1987, as the players trudged off the pitch following another defeat in the season's finale at the City Ground, hundreds of Newcastle United fans poured onto the pitch to celebrate a successful battle against relegation. One of those that made their way onto the pitch was yours truly and amongst the chaotic scenes, I asked big Tony for his shirt. Needless to say, I didn't return to Tyneside with my intended souvenir, but despite that I'm going to say big Tony was a cult hero of the eighties.

Shortly after securing another season in the top flight, Newcastle United parted company with Cunningham when he was sold to third division Blackpool for an unremarkable £25,000 in July 1987.

We all know that the fates often conspire in football circles and just a few months after that trip to Nottingham, me and some mates were following Tony Cunningham to the same seaside resort as Newcastle United played Blackpool in a League Cup second round, first leg encounter at Bloomfield Road.

That was the evening of 23 September 1987 and the trip was a blast.

The Housemartins' second album, 'The People Who Grinned Themselves to Death' had just been released and that was the soundtrack as we made our way across the Pennines. Heavy drinking as well as some recreational drug use by a number of those that made the trip, a combination of alcohol and magic mushrooms not mixing terribly well with the attractions on offer at the Pleasure Beach. This being the late 1980s, this was inevitably followed by an altercation outside the ground, although it was with a group of fellow Geordies twice our age, a case of mistaken identity.

That night, big Tony turned into a villain at Bloomfield Road.

On the stroke of half-time, a wayward back-pass from none other than Paul Gascoigne inadvertently played Cunningham clean through. Our former groundbreaking striker took full advantage of Gazza's mistake, slotting the ball home to give Blackpool a 1–0 victory.

To add insult to injury, some of the lads were still tripping after the game and went AWOL, needing to find alternative arrangements to get home after our driver refused to hang about.

In the second leg at St James' Park, Blackpool scoring early to take a 2-0 aggregate lead, although goals from Paul Goddard, Mirandinha, Darren Jackson and Gazza, atoning for his mistake in the first leg, gave United a 4-1 win on the night and with it, a passage into the next round.

Whilst Tony Cunningham was only on Tyneside for a little over two years before his move to Blackpool, it's fair to say he more laid the foundation for everything that followed in breaking down those hideous barriers that existed for black players of the era, and without big Tony taking those initial, heavy blows, I think the paths that superstars like Andy Cole and Les Ferdinand took in the next decade would have been infinitely harder.

articles.title: Fifteen Navy enlistees will face obstacle courses at Orlando Spartan Weekend
articles.summary: Navy enlistees and special operations teams are set to face obstacle courses during the Orlando Spartan Weekend.
articles.body:
Fifteen local Navy enlistees are expected to tackle obstacle courses at Orlando Spartan Weekend in Lake Nona this weekend, according to Navy representatives.

The event is scheduled for Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 10-11, at 6955 Lake Nona Blvd.

Spartan races combine running with obstacles that require competitors to climb, crawl and jump, testing strength and endurance.

Some of the participating enlistees have qualified for Navy special operations roles, according to the Navy. The announcement did not specify which roles.

The Navy is also sponsoring the "Extra Mile," an optional extension that competitors can take on after completing the main racecourse.

Attendees can try a pull-up bar challenge and a reaction drill. Members of Navy special operations teams are also expected to attend throughout the weekend.

"The Spartan 'Extra Mile' reflects exactly the kind of mindset we look for in the U.S. Navy," said Rear Adm. James P. Waters, commander of Navy Recruiting Command.

articles.title: Jeff Hafley issues challenge to Dolphins pass rusher
articles.summary: The Miami Dolphins finally got to the quarterback in Week 4, and now their coach has a challenge for one of their top pass rushers.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins went three weeks without taking down a quarterback, but in Week 4 against the Minnesota Vikings , Miami's front sacked former first-overall pick Kyler Murray four times, pushing the offense back 34 total yards.

Among those who were effective at getting after the quarterback on Sunday for the Dolphins was linebacker Chop Robinson, who finished the game with three quarterback hits and a sack. While this was a strong performance for the former first-round pick, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley issued a challenge to the pass rusher on Wedensday.

"He's confident," Hafley said. "I talked to him about it last night. He's getting into a rhythm. He's playing again, and he's playing fast. He's practicing fast, and he understands that how he prepares is how he's going to play. That was really the topic of our conversation. I wasn't surprised that he played well because of the way he practiced. Now, can he do it again? That's the challenge. Can he go out and practice that way to give him a chance to play the same way he did because if he doesn't, he won't.

"Now, it's time to put the pressure [on him]. I got it. Congrats. You had your 10 pressures and your sack. I love it. But can you do it again? Because if you don't then it doesn't matter. The only way to do that is to come out today and have the best practice he's had all year because now people are going to be watching him, and they're going to be trying to get after him a little bit just like we talked about at tight end. There are going to be some teams that say 'I'm not going to let Chop have a sack,' and it might open it up for somebody else. That's how the game works, so he has to go out today, and he's got to have a great practice."

Miami will take on the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday for an AFC showdown, and the Dolphins' front will need to get after quarterback Joe Burrow, especially if wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are healthy enough to play.

Cincinnati has allowed sacks on 5.42% of their dropbacks, which is the 14th-best rate in the league.

articles.title: Rhamondre Stevenson, Mack Hollins set to miss practice for Patriots
articles.summary: The Patriots are set to open the practice week without a couple of key offensive players.
articles.body:
The Patriots are set to open the practice week without a couple of key offensive players.

Head coach Mike Vrabel said at his Wednesday press conference that running back Rhamondre Stevenson and wide receiver Mack Hollins are expected to sit out the team's first on-field work of Week 5.

Stevenson was injured late in last Sunday's win over the Bills. Vrabel did not specify the nature of what appeared to be a lower body injury, but word will come on the injury report. The Patriots worked out Jamaal Williams on Tuesday in a move that was likely related to the uncertainty about Stevenson's availability.

Vrabel also said that cornerback Christian Gonzalez will remain out of practice. He missed all of last week with a shoulder injury.

articles.title: What Did Heat Fans Learn from Miami’s First Preseason Game?
articles.summary: The NBA preseason kicked off with the Miami Heat taking on the Toronto Raptors in Quebec City. Although it was just preseason, Heat fans were excited to get...
articles.body:
The NBA preseason kicked off with the Miami Heat taking on the Toronto Raptors in Quebec City. Although it was just preseason, Heat fans were excited to get a first look at their new squad taking the court.

The Heat's starting five consisted of Davion Mitchell , Klay Thompson , Andrew Wiggins , Bam Adebayo , and their new superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo .

While these guys would only play a little over 13 minutes each, they gelled well together. Miami would win the first quarter 41-23. Though Kawhi Leonard didn't play for Toronto, they still sent out most of their starters, including Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett .

If the Heat proved anything on Saturday night, it's that they have plenty of shooters to space the floor around Giannis and Bam. Multiple times down the court, Giannis drew defenders' attention and found wide-open shooters. Antetokounmpo had seven assists, all seven on three-pointers.

Wiggins hit four three-pointers; Adebayo and Mitchell each hit one. Off the bench, Tim Hardaway Jr. went 3-for-3 from downtown.

Many question marks around the Miami Heat this season centered on their shooting, since their two premier players aren't particularly known for it. This could not be more wrong. In the first quarter, the Heat shot 52% from the field and 53% from beyond the arc. They scored 41 points and hit seven three-pointers.

Antetokounmpo's natural gravity opened up many of these three-point looks. In the preseason opener, Wiggins arguably benefited most from this force. Antetokounmpo assisted Wiggins on four three-point makes, drawing up to three defenders at a time and drawing all 10 Raptors' eyes multiple times.

"He's someone that as soon as he steps on that court, you know, that gravitational pull towards him is insane. Because he's someone you got to really game plan for. Giannis is one of those ones," Wiggins said .

Outside of Bill Simmons, most of the NBA world knew that, if anything, the Miami Heat would have a stellar defense.

"Who's playing defense on this team? Who's guarding Jayson Tatum ?" Simmons asked .

Davion Mitchell clapped back , "That was definitely the worst take of the entire offseason."

Questioning Miami's spacing, shooting, depth, okay…but defense? The Heat are stacked from top to bottom with defense-minded guys. Antetokounmpo, Adebayo, Wiggins, Mitchell, and Pelle Larsson , to name a few, are a nightmare lineup for any opposing offense in the association.

The Heat defense proved themselves in their first preseason game. They blocked seven shots and forced 19 turnovers, but the ability to switch, help, and transition defensive stops to offensive scores was very appetizing to see for Heat fans.

On one possession in particular, Miami ran a small-big screen perfectly, with Adebayo stunting, which let Mitchell get back to the ball handler after being screened. Klay Thompson then closed out on the shooter and peel-switched with Mitchell. The Raptors' final resort on this possession was an isolation against Mitchell, nicknamed "off-night," which resulted in an airball.

This possession, like many others, showed the Heat's fluidity and ability to communicate effectively.

While Thompson's efforts did not show up in the box score, his defensive abilities were on full display in the almost 13 minutes he played.

Another offseason question was the Heat's depth. After losing two starters, the backup center, a Sixth Man of the Year runner-up, and a backup point guard, many said the Heat had no role players to back up Antetokounmpo and Adebayo.

Miami would sign shooters Thompson and Hardaway Jr., draft Ryan Conwell from Louisville, sign undrafted free agent Tre Donaldson from the University of Miami, and sign center Nick Richards .

Beyond these solid signings, Miami still has plenty of depth from last season. One player of note is Pelle Larsson. The Swedish guard signed an extension with Miami this offseason. Larsson had a great summer playing for Sweden's FIBA World Cup team.

As a possible 6-MOTY candidate, he is Miami's premier role player. Against Toronto, Larsson recorded 13 points on a perfect 3-for-3 from the field and 7-for-7 from the foul line.

Larsson finished with a +16, leading Miami's second unit. Antetokounmpo praised this group after the game.

"I was actually caught off guard during the game; once they went in, they were like, they were better than us, you know, they were better than the first unit," Antetokounmpo said . "In order for you to be good and have, you know, a good season, you gotta have a deep team."

Miami and their second unit clearly proved this in Quebec City. Hardaway Jr. looked great off the bench, and so did Nikola Jovic . Jovic, who has had an up-and-down time in Miami, scored 11 points in 17 minutes. He finished with a +11 rating, seven rebounds, four assists, and two blocks.

The Miami Heat resume preseason action on October 8th versus the New Orleans Pelicans. This will be Miami's first home game as they continue to prepare for the regular season.

articles.title: The Kids Are Alright: Mauricio Pochettino’s USMNT 2.0 Era Gets Off to a Fantastic Start
articles.summary: The United States men’s national team went a perfect 4-0 to kick off the 2030 cycle. A new era has brought new faces and, more importantly, there are real ob...
articles.body:
The United States men's national team went a perfect 4-0 to kick off the 2030 cycle. A new era has brought new faces and, more importantly, there are real objectives for Mauricio Pochettino's side on the horizon.

When the final whistle sounded in the United States men's national team's sluggish 1-0 win over Canada, it marked the end of the first camp of the 2030 cycle, and for Mauricio Pochettino , it could not have gone much better.

The USMNT won all four of its games, scoring 12 goals, allowing just three, and recording two consecutive shutouts. Oh, and one of those wins was a 3-0 dismantling of Mexico.

The biggest takeaway from the camp is that the young faces Pochettino brought into the squad came to play. All of the main names of the camp had strong performances: Cavan Sullivan , Julian Hall , Justin Ellis , Mathis Albert , Neil Pierre , Diego Kochen , and Brian Schwake all passed their first major test with flying colors.

It was exactly what Pochettino needed to kick off his new era: new faces, big wins, and, most importantly, some calm before his next true competitive test of the new cycle in the CONCACAF Nations League .

Here are some important assessments from the first big camp of the 2030 USMNT cycle.

The future Manchester City player and current Philadelphia Union star came to play. Cavan Sullivan was all over the field in the games he played and scored his first senior team goal against Mexico to truly announce his arrival on the USMNT.

While there are huge expectations surrounding the 17-year-old Sullivan, calm and patience should be the number one priority. He showed no fear and a drive that really impressed. Now, the thought of seeing him and Christian Pulisic on the same field can only spark more excitement for USMNT fans.

Pochettino will have a lot to think about for his next camp, as Julian Hall and Justin Ellis were both really impressive during the four-game stretch. Both found ways to score and impact games through their best attributes.

While Folarin Balogun and Ricardo Pepi are still the country's top two strikers, both Hall and Ellis will surely have them looking over their shoulders.

Philadelphia Union defender Neil Pierre has all the tools to become a future star for the USMNT and in Europe. Tall and comfortable on the ball, the big man is still going through a learning curve, but has everything necessary to be playing in a top European league sooner rather than later.

Aside from the aforementioned names, other players who upped their stocks were Diego Kochen, Auston Trusty , Sebastian Berhalter , and Mathis Albert.

Gio Reyna's camp was overall solid as well, despite his on-again, off-again style of play, but Pochettino can rest easy knowing he has plenty of players capable of challenging some of the core names on this team.

Zavier Gozo . A lot was expected from the new Crystal Palace winger, and for a long time, he was the standout player among the young crop. But Gozo saw action in just one game, a mixed-bag performance against Peru.

Still young and with plenty of talent, Gozo not playing in three straight games was very surprising.

Alex Freeman has looked better and better with every game he plays for the USMNT. Still just 22, he seems to have cemented his starting spot with Villarreal , who continue to bring the Baltimore native along slowly.

At times, that may frustrate USMNT fans, but Freeman has the makings of a very special player. Now playing in La Liga and continuing to hone his skills, Freeman is looking more and more like the definitive starting right back for the USMNT.

If there is one thing this camp has shown us, it is that there is some serious material for growth within the USMNT. There are still questions to be answered regarding the goalkeeping situation and what Pochettino believes his strongest XI looks like when factoring in his "kids," but the team clearly needs to internally, at the very least, outline its objectives.

First of all, the Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti won't be a cakewalk, but the U.S. can go into that match with plenty of confidence following a strong set of performances.

In addition, Pochettino is basically coaching the team we could very well see in its entirety at the Summer Olympics in 2028. Given the talent available, the U.S. should contend for a medal, and winning one would be a major success.

The CONCACAF Nations League is also there to be won, especially after victories over Mexico and Canada. Reestablishing regional dominance must be on the to-do list, and that will be the first major assignment for Pochettino and his team in the 2030 cycle.

The new-look USMNT got the Pochettino 2.0 era off to a bang. And for the first time in a long time, there is real optimism about what this team can build, now in the hands of a very capable manager.

articles.title: Dan Quinn: Marcus Mariota’s return expected sooner than later, no need for IR
articles.summary: Dan Quinn gives injury and roster updates as they prepare to host the Giants
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders are home from their international game in London against the Indianapolis Colts. They lost the game, and injuries to Marcus Mariota (MCL) and Jaylin Lane (ankle/IR) deflated the team. Dan Quinn has said they plan on having Jayden Daniels back as a full participant with the expectation he can start this week at home vs the Giants. Daniels will be wearing a brace when he plays, and Quinn said they've talked about protecting the elbow. He traveled with the team and was limited in practice last week, but wanted to play.

Marcus Mariota's MCL sprain is expected to follow the same timeline as the one that sidelined him in the preseason. Quinn said they are hopeful he can return after missing next week, and then having the bye before the team returns in Week 8 for a home game rematch against the Philadelphia Eagles. The team didn't place Mariota on injured reserve which would have kept him out for four games. Washington had QB Jack Plummer in for a workout, but seems confident in Jayden Daniels and Athan Kaliakmanis being available this week.

The Commanders announced that three players who have been on injured reserve for the first four games have returned to practice, and their 21-day windows have opened. CB Trey Amos (ankle), DE Deatrich Wise (quad), and RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) will have their individual recovery plans as they return to the field. Quinn was asked about a return timeline for Amos, and he noted he has only practiced once since breaking his leg as a rookie.

Quinn was asked about struggling players like CB Mike Sainristil and C/G Nick Allegretti having reduced roles and getting less snaps. He said they're working on the best scenarios for each player and they would make moves to improve the team. He mentioned Allegretti missing time in training camp, and other injuries that have limited him as he moved to center. He has now been replaced by free agent signing Lucas Patrick at center, and rookie Matt Gulbin at right guard.

articles.title: Bengals dealt worrisome update on Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins before Week 5
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have received injury updates on Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins ahead of their Week 5 matchup.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals are dealing with uncertainty around two of their biggest offensive weapons heading into NFL Week 5.

Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both suffered injuries during Sunday's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Their status will be closely watched as Cincinnati prepares for its next matchup.

The Bengals cannot afford to lose either receiver for an extended period. The latest updates on Chase and Higgins provide a clearer picture of their situations heading into this week.

Ja'Marr Chase enters concussion protocol

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images

Ben Baby of ESPN reported that Chase is in the NFL's concussion protocol after suffering an injury against the Jaguars. The star wide receiver will now go through the league's required evaluation process.

Chase finished Sunday's game with three receptions for 27 yards before leaving the contest.

He will need to progress through the necessary steps and receive clearance before returning to action.

Tee Higgins will practice despite adductor injury

Higgins received a more encouraging update ahead of Week 5. Baby reported that the Bengals wide receiver will practice Wednesday but will be limited because of an adductor injury.

Higgins was a major part of Cincinnati's offense against Jacksonville, catching 11 passes for 157 yards. His performance could become even more important if Chase is unable to play this week.

articles.title: Soumare credits togetherness for Stoke's revival
articles.summary: Stoke City's four wins from five has been helped by the growing togetherness in the squad, says summer signing Djibril Soumare.
articles.body:
Stoke City midfielder Djibril Soumare says the togetherness in the squad has helped turn their early season form around.

After losing their first three games of the Championship season, the Potters have rallied excellently, winning four of five matches before the international break to move into seventh place, two points off the top two.

Soumare, one of a number of key summer arrivals that included £10m Northern Ireland midfielder Ethan Galbraith , has been an impressive presence in Stoke's run and the former Sheffield United loanee said there was a simple reason for that.

"I felt love since day one. So I'm really enjoying it here," he told BBC Radio Stoke.

"I think that togetherness is really like a family on the pitch, out of the pitch. I said when I joined I still want to develop and the staff here, coaches - it was the right one for me I think.

"If it's time to be serious we're going to be serious but in the dressing room, having a laugh with the boys, is something special."

Soumare made 25 appearances for the Blades in the Championship last season and he said he returned to England from Portuguese club Braga this summer with more of an idea what to expect.

"There's still a lot to develop on my football - the intensity, because I think I'm not 100% fit yet as I didn't have a proper pre-season," he added.

"That season [with United] wasn't perfect but I learned a lot - it was my first year in England, so now I think I understand the league better and will enjoy it more.

"To be honest, I really love this team, so I'm really looking forward to score my first goal - that will be something really special for me."

Stoke return to Championship action on Saturday at Bolton Wanderers [15:00 BST].
